wire|mannequin.fact: "Mannequin" is on Wire's debut album Pink Flag (1977), produced by Mike Thorne at Advision Studios in London. The album packs 21 songs into about 35 minutes, since Wire stopped each song as soon as it had said what it needed to.

lunar vacation|tom.fact: "Tom" appears on Lunar Vacation's album Everything Matters, Everything's Fire (September 2024, Keeled Scales), produced by Drew Vandenberg. Singer Gep Repasky originally named the song after Tom Schwartz of Vanderpump Rules, and the band, who grew up together as childhood friends, call Decatur, Georgia home.

corridor|pow.fact: "Pow" is from Corridor's third album, Junior (October 2019), which made the Montreal band the first Francophone act signed to Sub Pop. It was the third single released from the album, following "Topographe" and "Domino," and is driven by jittery hi-hats and booming tom-tom offbeats.

wolf parade|shine a light.fact: "Shine a Light" is on Wolf Parade's debut album, Apologies to the Queen Mary (September 2005, Sub Pop). It also appeared on the band's self-titled 2005 EP, and the album is now regarded as a landmark of mid-2000s indie rock.

mitski|if i leave.fact: "If I Leave" is track four on Mitski's 2026 album Nothing's About to Happen to Me and came out as a single the same day as the album (February 27, 2026, Dead Oceans). Jared Hogan directed the video, which shows Mitski and her band performing in an abandoned house.

sharon van etten|comeback kid.fact: "Comeback Kid" was the lead single from Sharon Van Etten's fifth album, Remind Me Tomorrow (January 2019, Jagjaguwar), produced by John Congleton. The album marked a big shift in her sound, moving from guitar and piano toward synthesizers, organs, and harmoniums.

yves jarvis|bootstrap jubilee.fact: "Bootstrap Jubilee" was the lead single from Yves Jarvis' album The Zug (May 2022, ANTI-/Flemish Eye). Jarvis has said it was inspired by the films Paris, Texas and Boyhood and marks his 25th year on earth.

ween|push th' little daisies.fact: "Push th' Little Daisies" is from Ween's third album, Pure Guava (November 1992), and was released as a single in 1993. It got a big boost after MTV's Beavis and Butt-head commented on the video, and it reached number 21 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart.

the english beat|tears of a clown.fact: The English Beat (known simply as The Beat in the UK) turned Smokey Robinson and the Miracles' "The Tears of a Clown" into a ska song in 1979, and it reached number 6 in the UK. It was the band's first single and helped launch the British ska revival, then appeared on their 1980 debut album I Just Can't Stop It.

the tubs|who s gonna love you now?.fact: "Who's Gonna Love You Now?" is the lead single from Hard Life (2026, Merge Records), the third album by London band The Tubs, following 2025's Cotton Crown. Singer Owen Williams describes it as a Northern Soul-inspired pop song with organs, influenced by the Australian band Royal Headache.

jane remover|lips.fact: "Lips" was released in August 2023 as a single ahead of Jane Remover's second album, Census Designated (October 2023, DeadAir Records). Jane followed it with the 2025 album Revengeseekerz.

frankie cosmos|vanity.fact: "Vanity" was the lead single from Frankie Cosmos' sixth album, Different Talking (June 2025, Sub Pop). Greta Kline started writing it while walking about six and a half miles from Tompkins Square Park to Sunset Park in New York City.

matt berninger featuring phoebe bridgers.fact: Matt Berninger and Phoebe Bridgers recorded this for the Netflix film Between Two Ferns: The Movie, and it became the first single from Berninger's 2020 solo debut Serpentine Prison, which was produced and arranged by Booker T. Jones. Berninger, the National's singer, has jokingly called it "a love song between a spider and a moth."

bjork|i miss you.fact: "I Miss You" was the sixth and final single from Björk's second album, Post (1995), released in February 1997 on One Little Indian. Björk wrote and produced it with Howie B.

franz ferdinand|night or day.fact: "Night or Day" is a single from Franz Ferdinand's 2025 album The Human Fear. The Scottish band broke through with their self-titled 2004 debut album, which was led by "Take Me Out."

nick cave and the bad seeds|i let love i.fact: "I Let Love In" is on Let Love In, Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds' eighth studio album (April 1994, Mute Records), recorded between September and December 1993. The album produced three singles: "Do You Love Me?", "Loverman," and "Red Right Hand."

cafune|perspective.fact: "Perspective" was released in March 2023 as the first new music from the New York duo Cafuné (Sedona Schat and Noah Yoo) since they signed to Elektra Records and their viral hit "Tek It." It was co-produced by Imad Royal, who has also worked with Doja Cat and Carly Rae Jepsen.

austra|anywayz.fact: "Anywayz" opens Austra's 2020 album HiRUDiN, named after a peptide from leeches that is the most potent anticoagulant known. It was the first Austra record made with outside producers, Rodaidh McDonald and Joseph Shabason, and was recorded in the Spanish countryside.

buzzcocks|everybody's happy nowadays.fact: "Everybody's Happy Nowadays" was a 1979 Buzzcocks single, backed with "Why Can't I Touch It?", released a few months before their third album, A Different Kind of Tension (September 1979, United Artists). The song was meant ironically, though some fans thought the band had sold out when Pete Shelley played it on Top of the Pops.

at|punish my mind.fact: "Punish My Mind" is the second single from Autosmile, the 2026 album on 4AD by the Philadelphia electronic-folk duo @. It pairs mellow vocal harmonies with a calm acoustic guitar and woodwind arrangement that's interrupted by a monkey screech.

alabama shakes|garden.fact: "Garden" is from Alabama Shakes' 2026 album I Must Be Dreaming (August 2026), their first since 2015's Sound & Color, after a hiatus that ended in late 2024. The song showcases the quieter, more sensual side of Brittany Howard's voice.

babe rainbow|inner space.fact: "Inner Space" was released in September 2022 and opens Babe Rainbow's The Organic Album. The Byron Bay band trades some of its laid-back feel for a jet-propelled rhythm and spacey, hazy psychedelia.

king gizzard and the lizard wizard|alien.fact: "Alien Metal" is the title track of King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard's 28th album, surprise-released in August 2026 on their own p(doom) Records. It's their first hard electronic album, made entirely on a modular synthesizer rig the band nicknamed Nathan, which they've been using for their rave shows.

hana vu|alone.fact: "Alone" is the third track on Hana Vu's album Romanticism (May 2024, Ghostly International). It's one of the album's upbeat, lush moments, with soaring electric guitar riffs and a strummy guitar underneath.

panda bear and sonic boom|a ? of when.fact: The title track of Panda Bear and Sonic Boom's second album together (2026, Domino), following their 2022 debut Reset. The record is built from loops of harp by Mary Lattimore, steel drum sequences, pedal steel from Zena Kay, and even bits of a mariachi band.

wild nothing|shadow.fact: "Shadow" was the first song released from Wild Nothing's second album, Nocturne (August 2012, Captured Tracks). It features a string section, something bandleader Jack Tatum says he never could have done on his earlier home recordings without a proper studio.

bar italia|omni shambles.fact: "omni shambles" is a two-minute rocker from bar italia's 2025 album Some Like It Hot on Matador Records. The London trio is Nina Cristante plus Jezmi Fehmi and Sam Fenton, who also play together in the band Double Virgo.

cut worms|windows on the world.fact: "Windows on the World" is the lead single from Cut Worms' fourth album, Transmitter (March 2026), recorded in Chicago at Wilco's studio The Loft with Jeff Tweedy producing. Tweedy plays electric guitars and bass on the song and Wilco drummer Glenn Kotche adds percussion, after the band toured with Wilco in 2024.

stereolab|metronomic underground.fact: "Metronomic Underground" is the eight-minute opening track of Stereolab's 1996 album Emperor Tomato Ketchup. Although its sound is often credited to producer John McEntire of Tortoise, the band actually recorded it before they went to Chicago to work with him.

jamie xx|all you children (ft. the avala.fact: On "All You Children" Jamie xx teamed up with Australian sample-collage pioneers The Avalanches. He has said their approach to piecing together different sounds has always been an inspiration, and that working with them showed him new ways of making music.

washed out|feel it all around.fact: "Feel It All Around" was a defining song of the chillwave sound and became the theme song of the IFC sketch comedy show Portlandia, which premiered in January 2011. It first appeared in 2009 and samples the 1983 song "I Want You" by Italian singer Gary Low.

jane remover|fling.fact: "Fling" was released in October 2023 from Jane Remover's second album, Census Designated, on DeadAir Records. It came before their 2025 follow-up Revengeseekerz, which mixes digicore, EDM, hyperpop, and experimental hip-hop.

anna calvi|god's lonely man (feat. iggy.fact: This track opens Anna Calvi's 2026 EP Is This All There Is? on Domino Records, a four-song project where each track features a different collaborator: Iggy Pop, Matt Berninger, Laurie Anderson, and Perfume Genius. Calvi and Iggy Pop also star together in the music video, directed by Luigi Calabrese.

billy london|woman.fact: Billy London was created in 1978 when American-born musician Billy Barth moved to Britain to embrace its pop and punk scene. "Woman" was a 1981 single for RSO/Polydor produced by Nigel Gray, and it was rediscovered on the 2025 compilation All The Young Droids: Junkshop Synth Pop 1978-1985.

freak slug|if i could.fact: "If I Could" is the third track on Manchester-born artist and producer Freak Slug's second album, Amulet (September 2026, Future Classic). Its video was directed by St Clair Bryant with Pulse Films, and the track adds anthemic horns and an upbeat drum pattern to the record's hazy guitars.

japanese breakfast|the ballad of the wit.fact: Michelle Zauner's version of "The Ballad of the Witches' Road" comes from Marvel's Disney+ series Agatha All Along, where the song appears in several different cast versions. Co-produced by Jack Antonoff, her take has a sweeping, orchestral, Fleetwood Mac-style sound.

snail mail|my maker.fact: Lindsey Jordan first played "My Maker" in Seattle while touring with Dinosaur Jr. in 2025. She calls it the starting point for Snail Mail's third album, Ricochet, and shot its video in a hot air balloon, mostly in one take, co-directed with Elsie Richter.

brennan wedl|six o'clock news feat. waxa.fact: This is a cover of a Kathleen Edwards song, released in March 2026 to announce Brennan Wedl's signing to ANTI- Records. Wedl, originally from Minneapolis and now based in Nashville, first heard the original on a radio-station sampler CD around 2003, and Waxahatchee's Katie Crutchfield joined after the two bonded over loving Edwards's music.

baths|eden.fact: "Eden" was released as a single in January 2025 ahead of Baths' album Gut (February 2025). Baths is the project of Will Wiesenfeld, who debuted with Cerulean in 2010 on Anticon, and this track builds into a hooky dance-pop song before dissolving into strings.

radiohead|present tense.fact: "Present Tense" was written around 2008, and Thom Yorke first played it, then titled "The Present Tense," in a solo set at the UK's Latitude Festival in 2009. It was also performed with Atoms for Peace before Radiohead finally released it on A Moon Shaped Pool in 2016.

hana vu|22.fact: "22" is track four on Hana Vu's album Romanticism (May 2024, Ghostly International), which was produced with drums by Jackson Phillips of Day Wave. Vu has said the song is about being 22, feeling like both a baby and the oldest she'd ever been. A stripped-down version later appeared on her Movies EP.

jack white|g.o.d. and the broken ribs.fact: This song came out in April 2026 as a double single with "Derecho Demonico" and was later included on Jack White's album Frozen Charlotte (July 2026, Third Man Records). It features his live band: Patrick Keeler on drums, Dominic Davis on bass, and Bobby Emmett on keys.

jack white|derecho demonico.fact: "Derecho Demonico" came out in April 2026 as a double single with "G.O.D. And The Broken Ribs" and later landed on Jack White's album Frozen Charlotte (July 2026, Third Man Records). They were his first new songs since 2024's No Name, played with his live band of Patrick Keeler, Dominic Davis, and Bobby Emmett.

iron and wine|wait up.fact: "Wait Up" is on Iron & Wine's 2026 album Hen's Teeth (Sub Pop), Sam Beam's eighth full-length, and features the trio I'm With Her (Sarah Jarosz, Aoife O'Donovan, and Sara Watkins). The album was recorded in the same sessions as 2024's Light Verse, with the same band at Waystation studio in Laurel Canyon.

kelly lee owens|higher.fact: "Higher" was the third preview single from Welsh producer Kelly Lee Owens' fourth album, Dreamstate, following "Sunshine" and "Love You Got." Owens described each single as another taste of the feeling within the album.

the waterboys|fisherman's blues.fact: The title track of The Waterboys' 1988 album was recorded on the very first day of sessions that stretched from early 1986 to 1988, producing around 100 songs. Mike Scott moved to Ireland during the recording, and the album's folk and country blend was a big shift from the band's earlier grand rock sound; it became their best-selling record.

idles|grace.fact: "Grace" was released in December 2023 as a single from IDLES' fifth album, Tangk (February 2024), which was produced by Nigel Godrich, Kenny Beats, and IDLES guitarist Mark Bowen. Frontman Joe Talbot has said it was the only song whose words and singing came out of their sessions with Godrich, and it builds slowly into a big crescendo, softer than most IDLES songs.

siouxsie and the banshees|cities in dust.fact: "Cities in Dust" was the lead single from Siouxsie and the Banshees' 1986 album Tinderbox, released in October 1985. It reached number 21 in the UK, and its lyrics describe the ancient Roman city of Pompeii and its later excavation.

the mountain goats|candlebox.fact: "Candlebox" is from The Mountain Goats' 24th album, Days (August 2026), which John Darnielle originally planned to call Grunges as a spiritual sequel to 2017's Goths. The song follows a fictional bar band that lands a tour opening for '90s rockers Candlebox, and the real Mountain Goats then announced a tour with Candlebox.

rebounder|downtown people.fact: "Downtown People" is the title track and first single from the debut album by Rebounder, an NYC band made up of brothers Dylan and Noah Chenfeld. They made the record together, trading instruments and ideas in their windowless Greenpoint, Brooklyn studio, with small contributions from Jesse Rutherford and Gianluca Buccellati; it's out on Nettwerk.

bartees strange|lie 95.fact: "Lie 95" was the first single from Bartees Strange's third album, Horror (4AD), released in July 2024. It's a love song set along Interstate 95, the highway that runs from Florida to Maine, and the video follows him searching for love up the Northeast corridor.

avalon emerson|happy birthday.fact: "Happy Birthday" is the third track on Written into Changes (March 2026, Dead Oceans), the second album from Avalon Emerson & the Charm. Emerson, a DJ, road-tested the song in club sets at places like Berlin's Panorama Bar and Brooklyn's Nowadays before its release.

the flaming lips|a spoonful weighs a ton.fact: "A Spoonful Weighs a Ton" is from The Flaming Lips' 1999 album The Soft Bulletin, the record where the band moved toward lush, symphonic arrangements. The song sets a calm, orchestral feel against deep bass blasts.

hiatus kaiyote|telescope.fact: "Telescope" is the second track on Hiatus Kaiyote's 2024 album Love Heart Cheat Code (Brainfeeder/Ninja Tune). The Australian band built it on Brazilian, samba-like rhythms and was inspired by Hubble telescope photos taken on each band member's birthday, and it nods to The Temptations' "My Girl" in its vocal melody.

father john misty|i love you, honeybear.fact: The title track opens Father John Misty's second album, I Love You, Honeybear (February 2015, Sub Pop). Josh Tillman produced it with Jonathan Wilson, Phil Ek mixed it, and the album reached number 17 on the Billboard 200.

beirut|guericke's unicorn.fact: "Guericke's Unicorn" is from Beirut's album A Study of Losses, written for a stage show commissioned by the Swedish circus Kompani Giraff and inspired by Judith Schalansky's novel An Inventory of Losses. The title refers to a supposed fossil unicorn that was really reconstructed from the bones of animals like a mammoth and a narwhal.

gelli haha|klouds will carry me to sleep.fact: "Klouds Will Carry Me To Sleep" was released in March 2026 and added to the end of Gelli Haha's 2025 album Switcheroo on streaming services. The video was conceived by Gelli Haha and Sean Guerin and directed by David Gutel, and the song pairs singsong hooks with laser synths and a heavy low end.

deep sea diver|teardrop.fact: This is Deep Sea Diver's cover of Massive Attack's "Teardrop," the 1998 single from the album Mezzanine that featured Elizabeth Fraser of Cocteau Twins. The Seattle band released it in July 2026, produced by singer-guitarist Jessica Dobson and drummer Peter Mansen at their High Beam Studio, and Dobson says the original stopped her in her tracks as a kid.

kevin hambrick|black and blue.fact: Kevin Hambrick is a Fort Wayne, Indiana musician who was a fixture of the city's indie rock scene through the 2000s and 2010s. "Black and Blue" closes Refill, Part 1 (2024), a collection of previously unreleased b-sides, demos, and other recordings from 2004 to 2014.

tom waits|anywhere i lay my head.fact: This song comes from Tom Waits' 1985 album Rain Dogs. Scarlett Johansson later used it as the title of her 2008 debut album of Waits covers, produced by David Sitek of TV on the Radio, with David Bowie singing backing vocals on two tracks.

kim deal|nobody loves you more.fact: "Nobody Loves You More" is the title track of Kim Deal's debut solo album (November 2024), which she wrote and recorded over about a decade. It brings together current and former members of The Breeders, including her sister Kelley Deal, and its final sessions were at Steve Albini's Electrical Audio studio in Chicago.

my bloody valentine|honey power.fact: "Honey Power" is on My Bloody Valentine's Tremolo EP (February 1991, Creation Records), which topped the UK Indie Chart. Kevin Shields later joked that the EP really had seven tracks, but they called it four because "you're not allowed to" do that, so three short pieces went unnamed.

way dynamic|miffed it.fact: Way Dynamic is the songwriting project of Melbourne's Dylan Young, and "Miffed It" appeared in 2025 on his third album, Massive Shoe. The album brings in backing musicians on pedal steel, upright bass, and clarinet, and this song's hushed tone has been compared to Nick Drake.

mitski|lightning.fact: "Lightning" is the eleventh and final track on Mitski's eighth studio album, Nothing's About to Happen to Me, released in February 2026.

la luz|strange world.fact: "Strange World" was the first single from La Luz's album News of the Universe (May 2024), their first for Sub Pop. It opens with a murky, distortion-drenched guitar riff over pitter-pattering toms.

babe rainbow|waterfall.fact: "Waterfall" is a single from Babe Rainbow's seventh album, Acid and Honey (2026). The psychedelic band is from Byron Bay, New South Wales, Australia.

spiritualized|electricity.fact: "Electricity" was released as a single in July 1997 from Spiritualized's album Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space (June 1997), which NME named its Album of the Year. The album features guests including the Balanescu Quartet, the London Community Gospel Choir, and Dr. John.

spiritualized|soul on fire.fact: "Soul on Fire" was the first single from Spiritualized's sixth album, Songs in A&E, released in May 2008 on Sanctuary Records. The album blends art rock, neo-psychedelia, garage rock, and gospel.

laraw|kiss me on the floor.fact: "Kiss Me on the Floor" was released as a single in 2023 and appears on Laraw's 2024 album Quarter Life Crisis via Bravo musique. It was written by Lara Rawadi (Laraw) and Matt Kahane and produced by Quinton Sung and Laraw.

tame impala|eventually.fact: "Eventually" was released as a single in June 2015 ahead of Tame Impala's third album, Currents, which came out in July 2015.

lcd soundystem|x-ray eyes.fact: "x-ray eyes" was LCD Soundsystem's first new song since 2022's "New Body Rhumba," first heard on an NTS Radio show before its official release in late 2024. James Murphy wrote it with bandmates Al Doyle and Nancy Whang, and it was pressed on a limited-edition 12-inch with a "trash can dub" remix.

alexis taylor|out of phase (feat. lola k.fact: Hot Chip frontman Alexis Taylor's "Out of Phase" features actor-singer Lola Kirke and appears on his 2026 solo album Paris in the Spring (Night Time Stories). It was inspired by David Lynch, and the video, directed by Will Kindrick, was shot entirely on an iPhone.

lucid express|promise me.fact: Lucid Express is a dream-pop band from Hong Kong, and "Promise Me" is from their second album, Instant Comfort (2026). The music video, directed by Neo Yeung, was filmed over 24 hours during the 2025 Chinese New Year.

songs ohia|lioness.fact: "Lioness" is from Songs: Ohia's album The Lioness. Jason Molina recorded it at Chem19 Studio in Glasgow, Scotland, with his friends Aidan Moffat and David Gow of Arab Strap and Alasdair Roberts.

les savy fav|guzzle blood.fact: "Guzzle Blood" opens Les Savy Fav's 2024 album OUI, LSF, their first in 14 years, and was its second single. It's an urgent rocker with bursts of horns on the choruses and frontman Tim Harrington delivering his lines in clipped, half-rapped bursts.

ramones|rock 'n' roll high school.fact: The Ramones wrote this for the 1979 Roger Corman film Rock 'n' Roll High School, in which they starred. They first recorded it with producer Ed Stasium, then Phil Spector remixed it for the movie, and they later re-recorded it with Spector for 1980's End of the Century; it reached number 67 in the UK.

lime garden|i want to be you.fact: "I Want To Be You" is a single from Lime Garden's debut album One More Thing (February 2024, So Young Records), produced by Ali Chant. Singer Chloe Howard says it came from a memory of being 14 at her first gig and wondering whether she wanted to be like, or be with, someone on stage.

the jam|absolute beginners.fact: "Absolute Beginners" was a stand-alone single released in October 1981 that reached number 4 in the UK and never appeared on a Jam studio album. Paul Weller named it after Colin MacInnes' novel, one of his favorites, and the B-side was "Tales from the Riverbank."

remember sports|thumb.fact: "Thumb" is track three on Remember Sports' 2026 album The Refrigerator. Singer Carmen Perry wrote it from the perspective of her 15-year-old self, and the song strays from a standard pop structure with bursts of raucous distortion.

kurt vile|zoom 97.fact: "Zoom 97" opens Kurt Vile's tenth studio album, Philadelphia's Been Good to Me (May 2026), and was recorded at his home studio in Philly's Mount Airy neighborhood. It takes its inspiration from Lincoln Drive, the winding road through the area, with Mikel Patrick Avery on drums and Jesse Trbovich on background vocals.

king gizzard and the lizard wizard|hog c.fact: "Hog Calling Contest" is a rockabilly-flavored track from King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard's 26th album, Flight b741 (August 2024). The band says it began as one of their warm-up jams during the album sessions, and it's the only one they ever actually recorded.

king gizzard and the lizard wizard|field.fact: "Field of Vision" was the last single released before King Gizzard's 2024 album Flight b741. It gave its name to the band's own festival, Field of Vision, held in Buena Vista, Colorado, in August 2025.

hovvdy|blast.fact: "Blast" is a single from Hovvdy's sixth album, Big World, released on Arts & Crafts, and its video was directed by Michael Rees. On this record the Austin duo moves away from direct emotional statements toward more enigmatic songs about their place in the world.

militarie gun|b a d i d e a.fact: "B A D I D E A" was the lead single from Militarie Gun's second album, God Save the Gun (October 2025). Revolver reports that frontman Ian Shelton wrote it at the last minute, originally intending it for a hardcore record Doja Cat was planning.

loren kramar|hollywood blvd..fact: "Hollywood Blvd." was Loren Kramar's single announcing his signing to Secretly Canadian, an opulent '70s-style track with horns and bells about receiving a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Kramar directed the video himself, casting comedian John Early as a Hollywood studio tour guide.

death cab for cutie|riptides.fact: "Riptides" was the first single from Death Cab for Cutie's eleventh album, I Built You a Tower (June 2026, Anti- Records). It was released in March 2026 and is track nine on the album.

bon iver|jelmore.fact: "Jelmore" is from Bon Iver's fourth album, i,i (August 2019), and was released as a single in the weeks before the album alongside "Faith." At about two and a half minutes, it's one of the album's shorter tracks.

unknown mortal orchestra|ffunny ffrends.fact: Ruban Nielson uploaded "FFunny FFrends" anonymously to Bandcamp in May 2010, and within a day music blogs like Pitchfork were writing about it. He kept the project's identity secret at first because he wasn't sure what it should be, and the song later appeared on Unknown Mortal Orchestra's 2011 debut album.

khruangbin|a love international.fact: "A Love International" was the lead single from Khruangbin's fourth album, A La Sala (April 2024, Dead Oceans), whose title means "to the room" in Spanish. The trio recorded the album with no outside collaborators besides their engineer Steve Christensen, and the video was directed by Scott Dungate.

the only ones|another girl, another plan.fact: Written by Peter Perrett, "Another Girl, Another Planet" is the second track on The Only Ones' 1978 debut album and was recorded at Escape Studios in Kent, England. It didn't chart on release, but after appearing on the 1991 compilation The Sound of the Suburbs it was reissued and reached number 57 in the UK, and it's now the band's best-known song.

los campesinos!|feast of tongues.fact: "Feast of Tongues" was the first new music from Los Campesinos! since 2017 and the lead single from their album All Hell (July 2024, Heart Swells), their first in seven years. It's track six on the album.

elliott smith|ballad of big nothing.fact: "Ballad of Big Nothing" is from Elliott Smith's third album, Either/Or (February 1997, Kill Rock Stars). It was recorded mostly in Portland, Oregon while Smith was still a member of the band Heatmiser, and was produced by Smith with Tom Rothrock and Rob Schnapf.

justice|neverender (starring tame impala.fact: "Neverender" opens Justice's fourth album, Hyperdrama (April 2024), and features Kevin Parker of Tame Impala singing in falsetto. It won the Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Recording, and Parker and the French duo also teamed up on the album's "One Night/All Night."

fleet foxes|your protector.fact: "Your Protector" is on Fleet Foxes' self-titled debut album (June 2008, Sub Pop), which many critics ranked among the best albums of the 2000s. It was released as a single in 2009 and features flute alongside the band's signature vocal harmonies.

mount kimbie|dvd (feat. choker).fact: "dvd" is a 2022 collaboration between London duo Mount Kimbie, Dom Maker, and Michigan R&B singer Choker, from the double album MK 3.5: Die Cuts | City Planning. It features backing vocals from Sampha and piano from jazz musician Duval Timothy.

big thief|terminal paradise.fact: "Terminal Paradise" first appeared as the opening track of Big Thief singer Adrianne Lenker's 2018 solo album abysskiss. Big Thief later released their own version of the song too, including a live recording made at The Bunker Studio.

nothing|never come never morning.fact: "never come never morning" opens Nothing's 2026 album A Short History of Decay, recorded at Sonic Ranch, the legendary studio in Texas. The song's brass section was played by corridos musician Jesus Ricardo Ayub Chavira, whom the band met at the studio, and the horn players laid down their parts the very next morning.

the saints|(i'm) stranded.fact: "(I'm) Stranded" was recorded in Brisbane in June 1976 and released that September on the band's own Fatal Records label, making The Saints the first punk band outside the US to put out a record, ahead of the Sex Pistols and The Clash. It was written by guitarist Ed Kuepper and singer Chris Bailey, and rave reviews in Britain got them signed to EMI.

loving|blue.fact: "Blue" was released in October 2023 as the first new music from the duo Loving (Jesse Henderson and David Parry) since their 2020 debut album If I Am Only My Thoughts. The band has said the song was discovered like an old photograph in a journal, with the blueness and dizziness of a new love.

the white stripes|hello operator.fact: "Hello Operator" was the only single from The White Stripes' second album, De Stijl (2000), released with a cover of Dolly Parton's "Jolene" on the B-side. The album was recorded in a living room on an 8-track tape machine, and UK DJ John Peel picked the single as his "single of the week" even though it wasn't released in the UK.

stephen malkmus and the jicks|baltimore.fact: "Baltimore" is from Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks' 2008 album Real Emotional Trash and runs well over six minutes. Malkmus, the former Pavement frontman, has talked about the Baltimore references in its lyrics.

hiatus kaiyote|cinnamon temple.fact: "Cinnamon Temple" was released as a single in June 2024 ahead of Hiatus Kaiyote's fourth album, Love Heart Cheat Code. It has been described as equal parts noise rock, lo-fi, punk, soul, and prog.

telehealth|cool job.fact: "Cool Job" was the lead single from Seattle post-punk band Telehealth's second album, Green World Image (2026), released after they signed to Sub Pop. The band is led by married couple Alexander Attitude and Kendra Cox, and Attitude directed the video himself.

the damned|new rose.fact: "New Rose" was released in October 1976 by Stiff Records as the first single ever released by a British punk band, more than a month before the Sex Pistols' debut. Written by guitarist Brian James and produced by Nick Lowe, it was recorded in a single day at Pathway Studios in London, and its spoken intro parodies the Shangri-Las' "Leader of the Pack."

idles|gift horse.fact: "Gift Horse" was a single released in January 2024 ahead of IDLES' fifth album, Tangk, alongside "Dancer" and "Grace." The video was directed by David Helman, and the album was produced by Nigel Godrich, Kenny Beats, and IDLES member Mark Bowen.

kate bush|sat in your lap.fact: "Sat in Your Lap" was the first single from Kate Bush's 1982 album The Dreaming, released in June 1981, about 15 months before the album itself. It's built on a Fairlight CMI synthesizer, a Linn drum machine, and bamboo sticks that her brother Paddy Bush and the drummer swooshed from ten feet apart.

mountain man|rang tang ring toon.fact: "Rang Tang Ring Toon" is track four on Mountain Man's album Magic Ship (September 2018, Nonesuch Records). Its official video was directed by D.L. Anderson and filmed in Orange County, North Carolina, and the trio's close vocal harmonies carry the song.

lucy dacus|first time.fact: "First Time" appears on Lucy Dacus's third album, Home Video (2021), a song-by-song look back at her adolescence. Dacus has said she began writing it spontaneously while on a brisk walk, singing the melody to herself before it grew into a song about the rush of first love.

hospitality|friends of friends.fact: The music video for Hospitality's "Friends of Friends" premiered on Stereogum in January 2012 and was directed by Scott Jacobson, a writer for Bob's Burgers and The Daily Show. It starred Arrested Development actress Alia Shawkat alongside comedians Kurt Braunohler and Gabe Delahaye, following the on-screen unraveling of a long-distance relationship.

model/actriz|cinderella.fact: "Cinderella" was released in February 2025 as the lead single announcing Model/Actriz's sophomore album, Pirouette, following their breakout 2023 debut Dogsbody. The New York post-punk band, fronted by vocalist Cole Haden, dialed back some of their noisier tendencies on the track in favor of sleeker, club-ready grooves.

metz|light your way home.fact: METZ's "Light Your Way Home," from their 2024 album Up on Gravity Hill, features guest vocals from Amber Webber of Black Mountain. Guitarist Alex Edkins has said it was one of his favorite tracks to write, citing bands like Jesu and Low as sonic inspirations, and that Webber's vocal turn took the song "to another stratosphere."

woods|between the past.fact: "Between the Past" was released in 2023 as one of two lead singles (alongside "White Winter Melody") announcing Woods' album Perennial. Led by Jeremy Earl, the Brooklyn psych-folk band built the track around Beatles-esque wind instruments and a warm, hymn-like arrangement as the group approached its 20th year together.

destroyer|cue synthesizer.fact: For Destroyer's 2020 album Have We Met, Dan Bejar recorded all his vocals alone at night at his kitchen table, singing into a laptop microphone, then sent the files to longtime collaborator John Collins in Seattle to build the music around them. On "Cue Synthesizer," Bejar literally narrates the arrangement into being, calling out cues like "cue synthesizer" as if directing the song from the booth.

andrew bird|olympians.fact: "Olympians," from Andrew Bird's 2019 album My Finest Work Yet, grew out of an earlier instrumental called "Gotholympians" that first appeared on his 2013 live album Fingerlings before being reworked with new lyrics. The album itself was tracked with the full band playing together in the studio at once, letting the instruments' sound bleed across microphones rather than recording each part in isolation.

amber arcades|wouldn't even know.fact: "Wouldn't Even Know" comes from Dutch musician Annelotte de Graaf's 2017 EP Cannonball, released under her Amber Arcades project. The track was produced by Ben Greenberg and features additional vocals from Bill Ryder-Jones, formerly of the Coral.

tame impala|runway, houses, city, clouds.fact: Tame Impala's Kevin Parker recorded nearly all of the band's 2010 debut album Innerspeaker by himself at a remote beach shack called Wave House in Injidup, Western Australia. The sprawling, largely instrumental "Runway, Houses, City, Clouds" runs over seven minutes and closes the album with additional guitar from bandmate Dominic Simper, before the record was mixed by producer Dave Fridmann in New York.

beach house|heart of chambers.fact: Beach House wrote "Heart of Chambers," a highlight of their 2008 album Devotion, after noise complaints forced them out of their original practice spot at guitarist Alex Scally's house. They relocated to a new rehearsal space near Baltimore's I-83 highway, where the song came together.

shame|after party.fact: "After Party" is track nine on Shame's 2025 album Cutthroat, produced by John Congleton at Salvation Studios in Brighton. Its brooding electronic textures came from guitarist Sean Coyle-Smith's at-home experimentation, with singer Charlie Steen noting that Coyle-Smith and drummer Charlie Forbes brought a Depeche Mode-influenced electronic sound to the track.

frankie cosmos|aftershook.fact: "Aftershook" is a single from Frankie Cosmos' 2022 album Inner World Peace, the band's fifth LP for Sub Pop, blending 70s folk-pop with ambient and psychedelic touches. Bandleader Greta Kline has said the song is about processing the past while trying to hold onto "a balanced ratio of emotional awareness and hopefulness."

radiohead|i want none of this.fact: "I Want None of This" is a previously unreleased Radiohead track the band contributed to Help: A Day in the Life, a 2005 charity compilation for War Child. Alongside contributions from artists like Coldplay and Gorillaz, the album was written, recorded, and released within about a day, going on to become one of the fastest-selling download albums of its time.

suki waterhouse|good looking.fact: Suki Waterhouse first released "Good Looking" through Sub Pop in 2017 as the lead single from her debut EP, Milk Teeth. The song found a second life five years later when it went viral on TikTok in 2022, eventually reaching No. 14 on the US Hot Rock & Alternative Songs chart and earning platinum certification in the US.

paramore|burning down the house.fact: This is actually Talking Heads' 1983 single "Burning Down the House" from Speaking in Tongues. Drummer Chris Frantz said he got the title after seeing Parliament-Funkadelic's George Clinton work a crowd into chanting "burn down the house," and P-Funk keyboardist Bernie Worrell later played synthesizer and clavinet on the track; David Byrne wrote his vocal melody by improvising nonsense syllables over a jam by Frantz and bassist Tina Weymouth, a technique borrowed from producer Brian Eno. The song became Talking Heads' only US top-ten hit, peaking at No. 9.

iron & wine|jezebel.fact: "Jezebel" is a highlight of Iron & Wine's 2005 album Woman King, written by Sam Beam and produced with Brian Deck. The song borrows the name of the Biblical queen Jezebel but flips the script, reimagining her sympathetically as a wronged woman rather than the villain of the original story.

milly|spilling ink.fact: "Spilling Ink" is a single from Los Angeles alt-rock band MILLY's album Your Own Becoming, released via Dangerbird Records. Frontman Brendan Dyer said the band set out to write their fastest song yet, resulting in a track that rips through its riff and chorus in about two minutes.

eaves wilder|just say no!.fact: "Just Say No!" is the second track on British singer-songwriter Eaves Wilder's 2026 debut album, Little Miss Sunshine, released via Secretly Canadian. Wilder's sound on the record blends airy, ethereal vocals with fuzzed-out, shoegaze-adjacent guitars.

beck|say goodbye.fact: "Say Goodbye" was the third single from Beck's 2014 album Morning Phase, recorded largely live over just a few days in early 2013 in his hometown of Los Angeles. Beck told The Sun he was "making up the melody as you hear it" on the track, and critics likened its warm, Gram Parsons-style guitar work to Neil Young's Harvest.

the stone roses|she bangs the drums.fact: "She Bangs the Drums" was the second single from the Stone Roses' self-titled 1989 debut album and became the Manchester band's first UK Top 40 hit, peaking at No. 36. Ian Brown wrote the verse lyrics and John Squire the chorus, with the song generally described as being about the euphoria of falling in love.

summer twins|i will love you.fact: "I Will Love You" is a single by Riverside, California sister duo Summer Twins (Chelsea and Justine Brown), who formed in 2008 blending 1950s/60s girl-group and surf-rock harmonies with a dreampop haze. The song appears on their 2012 self-titled debut LP for Burger Records, and the band wrote, shot, and edited its own low-budget music video around their hometown of Riverside in February 2012.

mac demarco|passing out pieces.fact: "Passing Out Pieces" appears on Mac DeMarco's 2014 album Salad Days, whose title borrows a phrase from Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra referring to a carefree youth. Behind its warm, dreamy synth-pop, the song turns into a wry self-critique of the touring musician's life, opening with a line about how time away from home took its toll on him.

panda bear|praise.fact: "Praise" is a track from Panda Bear (Noah Lennox)'s 2007 album Person Pitch, written and recorded while Lennox was living in Lisbon, Portugal with his wife and young daughter. Like the rest of the record, the song was built up from layered, looped samples -- Lennox has said he typically started each Person Pitch track from around five source sounds before stacking his vocal harmonies on top.

angine de poitrine|fabienk.fact: "Fabienk" is a 2026 song by Angine de Poitrine, a Quebec math-rock duo -- guitarist "Khn" and drummer "Klek" -- formed in Saguenay in 2019, known for performing in costume as a stage persona. The song and its parent album, Vol II, won the Polaris Music Prize's companion song prize the same year.

man man|banana ghost.fact: "Banana Ghost" appears on Six Demon Bag, the 2006 sophomore album by Philadelphia experimental rock group Man Man, led by singer/keyboardist Ryan Kattner under the stage name Honus Honus. Six Demon Bag's carnival-esque blend of clattering percussion and theatrical vocals was what first pushed the band, formed in Philadelphia in 2003, into extensive national touring.

ladytron|city of angels.fact: "City of Angels" was released in October 2022 as the first single from Ladytron's 2023 album Time's Arrow, the band's first new music since 2019. Band member Daniel Hunt explained the song is "about forgetting... how fragile it is," blending imagery of different cities into one rather than describing any single real place.

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|vegemit.fact: "Vegemite" is a tongue-in-cheek 2014 single by Australian band King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, written and produced by frontman Stu Mackenzie as a two-and-a-half-minute ode to the salty Australian breakfast spread. It was released as a promo tie-in to the band's fourth studio album, Oddments, put out the same year on their own Flightless label.

elbow|station approach.fact: "Station Approach" comes from Elbow's 2005 album Leaders of the Free World and is a love letter to the band's hometown of Manchester, describing the rush of familiarity felt walking the road toward the city's Piccadilly train station after time away. It has become a fan-favorite live staple for exactly that homecoming feeling.

phosphorescent|revelator.fact: "Revelator" is the title track and lead single from Phosphorescent's 2024 album Revelator, singer-songwriter Matthew Houck's eighth studio album and his first for Verve Records. Houck has said finishing this song was what made him realize he was writing an entirely new record, one built around themes of coming home, partnership, and family.

mitski|geyser.fact: "Geyser" is the opening track and lead single from Mitski's 2018 album Be the Cowboy. Mitski has called it "one of my vaguest songs," explaining she wrote it about the sacrifices -- of relationships, opportunities, even health -- that come with committing to a music career, with the song's slow musical build mirroring its title.

beastie boys|no sleep till brooklyn.fact: "No Sleep till Brooklyn," a single from Beastie Boys' 1986 debut Licensed to Ill, features a guest guitar solo from Slayer's Kerry King, an unlikely rap-rock pairing that helped make it one of the group's signature tracks. Its title nods to Motorhead's live album No Sleep 'til Hammersmith, reworked into an ode to missing home while on tour.

wilco|taste the ceiling.fact: "Taste the Ceiling" is track six on Wilco's Star Wars, the band's surprise free album released in July 2015. The song was co-written by Jeff Tweedy and longtime touring collaborator Scott McCaughey, and critics singled it out as one of the record's gentlest, most classic-pop moments.

the national|hey rosey.fact: "Hey Rosey" grew out of a collaboration between The National and filmmaker Mike Mills that became the band's 2019 album I Am Easy to Find, released alongside a short film starring Alicia Vikander. Its lyrics were written by Carin Besser, wife of frontman Matt Berninger, and keyboardist Aaron Dessner has said Mills' suggestion to let the pianist improvise the song's opening reshaped its final arrangement.

bartees strange|backseat banton.fact: "Backseat Banton" is the closing track of Bartees Strange's 2025 album Horror, released via 4AD, and it arrived as the record's final pre-release single. Strange performed the song live on Jimmy Kimmel Live! ahead of the album's release.

perfume genius|it's a mirror.fact: "It's a Mirror" premiered in January 2025 as the lead single from Perfume Genius's seventh studio album, Glory, produced by Blake Mills. The song was described as a "ferocious rocker" built on dueling guitars, backed by a music video directed by Cody Critcheloe.

sylvan esso|coffee.fact: "Coffee" was the breakout 2014 single from Sylvan Esso's self-titled debut album, earning the North Carolina duo a national television performance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon that summer. Singer Amelia Meath has described the song as being about carving out a short personal break in an otherwise rushed day.

fiona apple|anything we want.fact: "Anything We Want" closes out Fiona Apple's 2012 album The Idler Wheel..., paired with "Hot Knife" to end the record on a hopeful note after its heavier songs. The song imagines an idealized moment of connection with a loved one, and Apple performed it with The Roots on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon just before the album's release.

wednesday|fate is....fact: "Fate Is..." opens Wednesday's 2020 sophomore album I Was Trying to Describe You to Someone, the Asheville band's first real step into the alt-country sound that would define their later work. Songwriter Karly Hartzman draws on Southern literary imagery to describe stubbornly facing up to the consequences of one's own choices.

spiritualized|crazy.fact: "Crazy" is a track from Spiritualized's 2022 album Everything Was Beautiful, released on Fat Possum Records, and features backing vocals from American country singer Nikki Lane. It was the second song revealed to the public ahead of the album's release.

talk talk|living in another world.fact: "Living in Another World" was a hit single from Talk Talk's 1986 album The Colour of Spring, written by Mark Hollis and Tim Friese-Greene. The track features a guest organ performance from Traffic's Steve Winwood, and the album went on to reach number eight on the UK charts.

bjork|army of me.fact: "Army of Me" was written and produced by Bjork with Graham Massey of 808 State, and served as the lead single for both her 1995 album Post and the soundtrack to the film Tank Girl. Its stomping industrial groove is built around a slowed-down sample of the drum break from Led Zeppelin's "When the Levee Breaks."

sufjan stevens|tell me you love me.fact: "Tell Me You Love Me" appears on Sufjan Stevens' 2020 album The Ascension, and its glimmering piano intro reworks a phrase from "Climb That Mountain," a track off his instrumental album Aporia. The song's music video was directed by filmmaker Luca Guadagnino, best known for Call Me By Your Name.

beirut|no no no.fact: Beirut recorded 'No No No' and the rest of the album together in just two weeks, tracking live in the studio with bassist Paul Collins and drummer Nick Petree in fall 2014. It was frontman Zach Condon's first new material after taking time off from touring, and the album came out on 4AD on September 11, 2015.

one step closer|giant's despair.fact: One Step Closer are a melodic hardcore band from Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania. Their song 'Giant's Despair,' from the 2024 album All You Embrace, builds to a roaring conclusion incorporating shimmering shoegaze guitars, towering drums, and triumphant horns, and its music video was shot around the band's Wilkes-Barre and Scranton hometowns.

lankum|newcastle.fact: Lankum's 'Newcastle' is their take on a centuries-old English folk tune first published in The English Dancing Master back in 1651. The Irish band learned their version from musician Sean Fitzgerald, who was taught it by his mother as a child, and it appears on their 2023 album False Lankum.

big thief|red moon.fact: 'Red Moon' comes from Big Thief's sprawling 2022 double album Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe In You, recorded across four different sessions from upstate New York to Topanga Canyon and Tucson. The song leans into an Appalachian folk sound, powered by a wailing fiddle from guest musician Mat Davidson, who records solo as Twain.

stereolab|the noise of carpet.fact: 'The Noise of Carpet' was the second single from Stereolab's 1996 album Emperor Tomato Ketchup, sitting at the album's midpoint as a callback to the band's earlier, rawer sound. It's built on a fuzzed-out guitar riff closer to the Velvet Underground than Stereolab's usual style, layered with wordless backing vocals from Laetitia Sadier, Mary Hansen, and Morgane Lhote.

real estate|easy.fact: 'Easy' is the lead track on Real Estate's 2011 album Days, which the New Jersey band recorded over five months in a barn in New Paltz, New York with producer Kevin McMahon. Its music video was released through Funny or Die and directed by comedian Tom Scharpling.

friko|crimson to chrome.fact: 'Crimson to Chrome' was the breakout single from Chicago band Friko, later included on their 2024 debut album Where We've Been, Where We Go From Here. It spent three weeks at No. 1 on the SiriusXMU chart and drew praise from outlets like Pitchfork and Brooklyn Vegan.

trembler|love leave the body.fact: 'Love Leave the Body' closes out Houston band Trembler's 2026 EP Total Sorry as an overdriven, shoegaze-tinged rocker built around a towering chorus. The band recorded and mixed the EP themselves at their own Shiny Tone Recordings, with mastering by Corey Coffman, who also produced their 2022 full-length Folding.

palace|gravity.fact: 'Gravity' is a slow-building, five-minute track from London band Palace's 2016 debut album So Long Forever. Critics noted its psychedelic, blues-tinged atmosphere, drawing comparisons to early Coldplay records like Parachutes and A Rush of Blood to the Head.

the avalanches|blue shadows (feat. karen.fact: 'Blue Shadows' reunited The Avalanches with Yeah Yeah Yeahs singer Karen O, following their 2020 collaboration 'Dial D for Devotion.' The track actually began years earlier as an idea from Avalanches member Andy Szekeres that was nearly forgotten until bandmate Tony Di Blasi rediscovered it in an old folder, and it marks the first time Karen O actually sings on an Avalanches track rather than reciting lyrics.

waxahatchee|hear you.fact: 'Hear You' appears on Waxahatchee's 2017 album Out in the Storm, released on Merge Records. The record features Katie Crutchfield's sister Allison on keyboards and percussion, alongside touring Sleater-Kinney guitarist Katie Harkin.

toro y moi feat. unknown mortal orchestr.fact: 'The Medium' pairs Toro y Moi's Chaz Bundick with Unknown Mortal Orchestra's Ruban Nielson, continuing a long friendship between the two artists -- Nielson previously contributed guitar to Toro y Moi's 2015 album What For?, and Bundick has covered UMO's 'Multi-Love' live. The song appears on Toro y Moi's 2022 album Mahal.

toro y moi|postman.fact: 'Postman,' from Toro y Moi's 2022 album Mahal, samples the 1980 disco track 'A Lover's Holiday' by Change. The psych-funk song rides a bouncy bassline and a breezy vocal from Chaz Bundick.

wild nothing|summer holiday.fact: 'Summer Holiday' was Wild Nothing's very first single, released on Captured Tracks at the end of 2009 before founder Jack Tatum had even settled on a full band. It later appeared on Wild Nothing's 2010 debut album Gemini, with lyrics drawn from Tatum's teenage memories.

squirrel flower|not me.fact: Ella Williams, who records as Squirrel Flower, has said 'Not Me' came to her after waking from a dream while staying in Silver City, New Mexico. She's cited the book Women Who Run With the Wolves as an inspiration, particularly its message about not settling for less than what you truly want.

kim gordon|play me.fact: The title track of Kim Gordon's 2026 album Play Me opens the record with a 1990s-inspired hip-hop beat and a horn section. Like her prior solo album The Collective (2024), Play Me was produced by Justin Raisen.

jungle|talk about it.fact: 'Talk About It' comes from Jungle's 2021 album Loving in Stereo, which found the London duo expanding their sound with disco strings and hard-hitting percussion layered under their signature falsetto harmonies. The album broadened Jungle's collaborator list beyond the group's core writing team.

latchkey kids|cower.fact: 'Cower' is by Latchkey Kids, a band formed by three friends -- Hanny, Joey, and Cyle -- in New Brunswick, New Jersey, who bonded over a shared love of bands like The Menzingers and Pinegrove. The song appears on their 2026 album Year of Summers.

wild pink|dulling the horns.fact: Wild Pink began writing 'Dulling the Horns' during soundchecks while touring behind their 2022 album ILYSM. For the resulting 2024 album of the same name, frontman John Ross chose to record live in the room with engineer Justin Pizzoferrato, aiming for a rawer sound and citing Weezer's Blue Album as a guitar-tone reference point.

father john misty|hollywood forever ceme.fact: 'Hollywood Forever Cemetery Sings' was the first single from Fear Fun, the 2012 debut album released under Josh Tillman's Father John Misty moniker. Its music video, which premiered on Entertainment Weekly's Music Mix blog, stars actress Aubrey Plaza of Parks and Recreation.

khruangbin|so we won't forget.fact: 'So We Won't Forget' appears on Khruangbin's 2020 album Mordechai, which marked a shift for the Texas trio toward songs with prominent lead vocals after years of largely instrumental music. It was one of the first Khruangbin tracks to put singing so clearly in the spotlight.

deep sea diver|shovel.fact: "Shovel" is a single by Seattle indie-rock band Deep Sea Diver, led by singer-guitarist Jessica Dobson, from their 2025 album Billboard Heart on Sub Pop Records. The song blends grunge grit with synth-pop, and its one-shot music video, co-directed by Dobson, was inspired by David Lynch, the Coen brothers, Nick Cave, and Kate Bush's dance moves.

ibibio sound machine|got to be who u are.fact: "Got to Be Who U Are" is a 2024 single by London-based Afro-funk group Ibibio Sound Machine, fronted by Anglo-Nigerian singer Eno Williams, released on Merge Records ahead of their album Pull the Rope. The track opens over a traditional African mbira pattern before dropping into a house-influenced dance groove, built around the idea that what unites people matters more than what separates them.

black belt eagle scout|i said i wouldn't.fact: "I Said I Wouldn't Write This Song" comes from Black Belt Eagle Scout's 2019 album At the Party with My Brown Friends, the project of Pacific Northwest musician Katherine Paul. Paul has said the song is about a feeling she didn't expect to write about but that ultimately had to come out, and its animated video draws on Northern imagery like cloudberry picking and Arctic landscapes.

hatchie|nosedive.fact: Australian dream-pop artist Hatchie (Harriette Pilbeam) wrote "Nosedive" with Joe Agius and Jorge Elbrecht after a night out at a Denver goth club, and the trio tried to bottle that club's energy, including an unusual lyric-free chorus. It became a standout single ahead of her 2022 album Giving the World Away.

arlo parks|too good.fact: "Too Good," from Arlo Parks' 2021 debut album Collapsed in Sunbeams, was written during one of her first sessions with producer Paul Epworth, known for his work with Adele and Florence + the Machine. Parks has said the track came together after she shared her eclectic influences with him, from 1970s Zambian psych-rock to MF DOOM and Tame Impala.

teenage fanclub|the concept.fact: "The Concept," written and sung by Norman Blake, was the second single from Teenage Fanclub's 1991 album Bandwagonesque on Creation Records. The sprawling six-minute track helped the Scottish band's album get named Spin magazine's Album of the Year for 1991, beating out Nirvana's Nevermind and R.E.M.'s Out of Time.

the magnetic fields|everything is one bi.fact: "Everything Is One Big Christmas Tree" appears on The Magnetic Fields' 2010 album Realism, a deliberately "back to basics," all-acoustic follow-up to their electronic record Distortion. The charmingly ramshackle holiday tune has been praised for sounding like the soundtrack to a half-remembered vintage animated Christmas special.

beach house|walk in the park.fact: "Walk in the Park" is a dream-pop track from Beach House's breakout 2010 album Teen Dream, written by the Baltimore duo Victoria Legrand and Alex Scally and produced with Chris Coady. It later got a stripped-down rework on the band's iTunes Session EP the same year.

tame impala|it is not meant to be.fact: "It Is Not Meant to Be" opens Tame Impala's 2010 debut album Innerspeaker, a one-man studio project written, played, and recorded almost entirely by Australian musician Kevin Parker. Much of the album was tracked at a beach house called Wave House Injidup in Western Australia, and this opening track's dreamy vocal drew comparisons to John Lennon.

pom pom squad|spinning.fact: "Spinning" is the lead single from Pom Pom Squad's sophomore album Mirror Starts Moving Without Me, the project led by New York songwriter Mia Berrin. Built on crystalline piano and a slow-shuffling beat, the song's video, co-directed by Berrin and Benjamin Lieber, is staged inside a surveillance-room set.

bat for lashes|kids in the dark.fact: "Kids In The Dark" comes from Bat for Lashes' 2019 concept album Lost Girls, on which Natasha Khan created an alter ego named Nikki Pink, heroine of an imagined 1980s girl-gang movie. Khan has said the song grew out of the feeling of driving through Los Angeles at sunset, giving its synth-pop sound an "us-against-the-world" romance.

m83|wait.fact: "Wait" is a shoegaze-leaning track from M83's 2011 double album Hurry Up, We're Dreaming, notably less electronic than the rest of the record, opening on acoustic guitar before building into cinematic, Sigur Ros-sized swells. It was released as the album's fifth single in December 2012 with a video directed by the duo Fleur & Manu.

radiohead|the gloaming. (softly open our.fact: Every song on Radiohead's 2003 album Hail to the Thief carries a two-part title, and "The Gloaming. (Softly Open Our Mouths in the Cold.)" is the eighth track, written by all five band members and produced with longtime collaborator Nigel Godrich. The title word "gloaming" is an old term for twilight or dusk.

weyes blood|everyday.fact: "Everyday," the second single from Weyes Blood's 2019 album Titanic Rising, channels a 1970s psychedelic-pop sound with an upbeat piano melody. Singer Natalie Mering has said the song is about the chaos and exhaustion of modern dating, likening it to everyone "sailing off onto ships to nowhere."

meat puppets|split myself in two.fact: "Split Myself in Two" is a fast, cowpunk-flavored track from Meat Puppets' influential 1984 album Meat Puppets II on SST Records. Clocking in at just over two minutes, it shows the Arizona trio still channeling the hardcore-punk energy of their earlier records even as they branched into country and psychedelia.

porridge radio|sick of the blues.fact: "Sick Of The Blues" is the lead single from English band Porridge Radio's 2024 album Clouds in the Sky They Will Always Be There for Me, written by frontwoman Dana Margolin with Sam Yardley and Georgie Stott. Margolin has said it's about being heartbroken and reclaiming your own joy rather than depending on someone else for it; its video, directed by Margolin's sister Ella, was filmed at Paris's Centre Pompidou.

goose|good2b.fact: "Good2B" is the first single from jam band Goose's 2026 album Big Modern!, released on their own label, No Coincidence Records. The band described the song as capturing a kind of joyful surrender amid modern-life chaos, calling it "a personal oasis in the algorithm."

beck|no distraction.fact: "No Distraction" is a reggae-funk flavored track from Beck's 2017 album Colors, built on a strummy chord progression he's said was partly inspired by the Police. He described writing it about the modern urge to be fully present with someone despite constant phone and screen distractions.

guided by voices|teenage fbi.fact: "Teenage FBI" was the first single from Guided by Voices' 1999 album Do the Collapse, recorded during the Dayton, Ohio band's brief run on a major label. The song later found new life placed in the TV shows Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Veronica Mars.

iron & wine|thomas county law.fact: "Thomas County Law" appears on Iron & Wine's 2017 album Beast Epic, the project of singer-songwriter Sam Beam. Beam has said the song is about "both denying and accepting one's origins," wrestling with an ambivalent relationship to where he's from.

alex g|gretel.fact: "Gretel" appears on (Sandy) Alex G's 2019 album House of Sugar and reworks the Brothers Grimm fairy tale from Gretel's point of view, giving it a darker, more cynical spin. The album's title itself was inspired by a short story called "The House Made of Sugar" by Argentine writer Silvina Ocampo, which Alex G said got stuck in his head while writing.

phantogram|attaway.fact: "Attaway" appears on Phantogram's 2024 album Memory of a Day, released via Neon Gold Records. The title is actually a made-up word the duo coined as a playful twist on the phrase "atta boy" or "there ya go." The track was produced with John Hill, part of a batch of collaborators the band brought in for the record.

queens of the stone age|easy street.fact: "Easy Street" is a 2026 single from Queens of the Stone Age featuring outlaw-country singer Nikki Lane, marking the band's first-ever official collaborative single. Josh Homme produced it with bandmate Michael Shuman, and they intentionally kept the recording loose and demo-like, leaving in tempo shifts and imperfect handclaps rather than polishing them out.

the brian jonestown massacre|anenome.fact: "Anenome" dates back to 1996 and was later included on The Brian Jonestown Massacre's 2004 compilation Tepid Peppermint Wonderland: A Retrospective, which introduced newer fans to deep cuts from the band's famously prolific catalog. Frontman Anton Newcombe was known for releasing multiple full albums in a single year during the band's 1990s heyday.

grizzly bear|speak in rounds.fact: "Speak in Rounds" comes from Grizzly Bear's 2012 album Shields. The band had spent months recording an entire album's worth of material in Marfa, Texas, but scrapped most of it; back at Ed Droste's grandmother's Cape Cod house, guitarist Daniel Rossen simply strummed by the fire while Droste sang, and songs like "Speak in Rounds" came together in that stripped-down setting. Droste's vocal take was recorded after he thought he had nothing left in the tank, giving it an unusually raw quality.

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|people.fact: "People-Vultures" is one of nine tracks on King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's 2016 album Nonagon Infinity, which was built so every song flows seamlessly into the next and the final track loops right back into the first, letting the whole record play forever without a break. The song's music video shows the band members merging into a giant "Person-Vulture" character who tangles with other creatures pulled from the album's other tracks.

low|sunflower.fact: "Sunflower" opens Low's 2001 album Things We Lost in the Fire, which the Minnesota trio recorded with famed engineer Steve Albini in Chicago before finishing touches were added back home in Minneapolis by Tom Herbers. The song is sung by married bandmates Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker, whose intertwined harmonies became one of the band's signature sounds.

future islands|the fight.fact: "The Fight" was released as the fifth single from Future Islands' 2024 album People Who Aren't There Anymore. It pulls back from frontman Samuel T. Herring's usual explosive stage energy in favor of a more delicate, introspective vocal delivery, set against Gerrit Welmers' shimmering synth textures.

boygenius|stay down.fact: "Stay Down" comes from boygenius's self-titled 2018 debut EP. Julien Baker, Phoebe Bridgers, and Lucy Dacus formed the group after bonding on a shared tour, then holed up at Sound City Studios in Los Angeles for just four days in June 2018, with each member bringing one nearly-finished song for the others to help build out. Baker's contribution became "Stay Down."

eels|last stop: this town.fact: "Last Stop: This Town" is a single from Eels' 1998 album Electro-Shock Blues, co-written and co-produced by frontman E with Michael Simpson of the Dust Brothers. Its offbeat music video, directed by Garth Jennings' company Hammer & Tongs and featuring vegetables strewn around the set, earned a Breakthrough Video nomination at the 1999 MTV Video Music Awards. The single reached number 23 on the UK charts.

grouper|alien observer.fact: "Alien Observer" is the title track of Grouper's 2011 album A I A: Alien Observer, one half of a two-album set released the same day alongside its companion, A I A: Dream Loss. Both records were self-released by Liz Harris on her own label, Yellow Electric, and built from layered, ghostly vocals and arpeggiated guitar recorded over several years.

mj lenderman|joker lips.fact: "Joker Lips" was released as the second single from MJ Lenderman's 2024 album Manning Fireworks, his first for ANTI- Records. Its music video, directed by Ben Turok, features Lenderman and his backing band, The Wind, performing on an overgrown North Carolina hillside.

rogue wave|kicking the heart out.fact: "Kicking the Heart Out" is the fifth track on Rogue Wave's 2004 debut album, Out of the Shadow, released on Sub Pop. Decades later, in 2026, Sub Pop gave the album an expanded reissue that paired the original tracks with newly unearthed four-track home demos, including an early version of this song.

mount kimbie|fishbrain.fact: "Fishbrain" is the seventh track on Mount Kimbie's 2024 album The Sunset Violent, the duo's first record made as a full four-piece band. The album also features London artist King Krule as a guest vocalist on two other tracks.

weird nightmare|baby don't.fact: "Baby Don't" appears on Hoopla, the 2026 sophomore album from Weird Nightmare, the melodic side project of Alex Edkins, better known as the frontman of noise-punk band METZ. Weird Nightmare trades METZ's abrasive volume for hooky, jangling pop-rock songwriting.

anna burch|what i want.fact: "What I Want" is track eight on Anna Burch's 2018 debut album Quit the Curse. It's been described as an anti-breakup song, with Burch taking a level-headed, mature approach and singing that she "won't play the victim" just because she didn't get what she wanted. Burch, a Detroit songwriter, had previously sung with Frontier Ruckus and co-fronted Failed Flowers before going solo.

the vaselines|dying for it.fact: "Dying for It" is the title track of the Scottish duo The Vaselines' 1988 EP, recorded at Pierhouse Studios in Edinburgh and released on 53rd & 3rd Records. Kurt Cobain named the EP one of his all-time favorite releases, and Nirvana went on to cover two of its other songs, "Molly's Lips" and "Jesus Wants Me for a Sunbeam."

cherry glazerr|had ten dollaz.fact: "Had Ten Dollaz" was the title track of a self-released, two-song digital EP Cherry Glazerr put out in 2014, while the band was still just starting out in Los Angeles. The EP's other song, "Nurse Ratched," was later re-recorded and included on the band's 2017 major-label debut album, Apocalipstick.

vampire weekend|diane young.fact: "Diane Young," from Vampire Weekend's 2013 album Modern Vampires of the City, gets its title from wordplay on the phrase "dying young." The track was produced by Rostam Batmanglij, Ezra Koenig, and Ariel Rechtshaid, and its striking music video shows two vintage Saab cars in slow motion, achieved by filming just five seconds of real footage at 1,000 frames per second with a high-speed Phantom camera.

the smiths|hand in glove.fact: "Hand in Glove" was The Smiths' debut single, released in May 1983 on Rough Trade Records and recorded for just L250 at Strawberry Studios in Stockport. Johnny Marr wrote the music and Morrissey the lyrics, with Marr adding a harmonica overdub. A year later, 1960s pop star Sandie Shaw recorded her own version backed by the Smiths, giving her first UK hit in a decade, and the band performed barefoot alongside her on Top of the Pops as a nod to her famous bare feet performances in the 1960s.

sufjan stevens|no shade in the shadow of.fact: "No Shade in the Shadow of the Cross" served as the lead single from Sufjan Stevens' 2015 album Carrie & Lowell, released digitally in February and then on a limited 7-inch through Joyful Noise Recordings. A neat production detail: the low static running through the track isn't manipulated tape hiss, but the actual sound of an air conditioner fan blasting on high in Stevens' apartment while he recorded.

angel olsen|ghost on.fact: "Ghost On" is track four on Angel Olsen's fifth studio album, Big Time, released in 2022 on Jagjaguwar. Olsen co-produced the record with Jonathan Wilson, who plays drums, guitar, and percussion on the song alongside bassist Emily Elhaj and guitarist Jake Blanton, with the whole album recorded at Wilson's Fivestarstudios in Los Angeles.

the jam|the modern world.fact: "The Modern World" was released as a single in October 1977, taken from The Jam's second album, This Is the Modern World. That album's tepid reception, plus a rough North American tour opening for Blue Oyster Cult, left frontman Paul Weller with such severe writer's block that the band scrapped its first batch of follow-up songs, regrouping to record the far more successful All Mod Cons the next year.

beabadoobee|take a bite.fact: "Take A Bite" is the lead single from beabadoobee's third studio album, This Is How Tomorrow Moves. She's said the song was partly inspired by an Elliott Smith song and partly by a "funky" rhythm she picked up from an Ashlee Simpson track.

rilo kiley|the frug.fact: "The Frug" appeared on Rilo Kiley's self-titled 1999 EP and namechecks a string of 1960s dance crazes, including the Frug, the Freddie, the Robocop, and the Smurf. It's a fitting subject for singer Jenny Lewis, who as a child actor danced both the Frug and the Freddie on-screen in the 1989 film Troop Beverly Hills.

the sugarcubes|regina.fact: "Regina" was the lead single from The Sugarcubes' second album, Here Today, Tomorrow, Next Week! (1989), and became the Icelandic band's biggest U.S. hit, reaching No. 2 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart.

unknown mortal orchestra|one at a time.fact: "One at a Time" appears on Unknown Mortal Orchestra's 2013 album II, a short, funky track built around a distorted wah guitar riff and thumping bassline that pays clear homage to Sly and the Family Stone. II went on to win Best Alternative Album at the 2013 New Zealand Music Awards.

nilufer yanya|mutations.fact: "Mutations" comes from Nilufer Yanya's 2024 album My Method Actor, recorded at Echo Zoo studio with producer Will Archer. Its music video was directed by Yanya's sister, Molly Daniel, and filmed along the streets and beaches of Spain.

the fixx|the sign of fire.fact: "The Sign of Fire" was released in November 1983 as a single from The Fixx's album Reach the Beach, following the band's breakout hit "One Thing Leads to Another." It peaked at No. 32 in the US and No. 20 on the mainstream rock chart.

ora the molecule|intergalactic dance.fact: "Intergalactic Dance" was shared ahead of Ora the Molecule's (Nora Schjelderup) 2025 album Dance Therapy. Schjelderup has said the song was partly inspired by Antoine de Saint-Exupery's novel The Little Prince, framing the track as a call to be unapologetically yourself.

friko|something worth waiting for.fact: "Something Worth Waiting For" is the title track of Friko's second album, released in April 2026 on ATO Records and produced by John Congleton. It's the follow-up to their acclaimed 2024 debut, Where We've Been, Where We Go From Here; the core duo of drummer Bailey Minzenberger and vocalist Niko Kapetan expanded to a four-piece, adding guitarist Korgan Robb and bassist David Fuller for this album cycle.

the beths|silence is golden.fact: "Silence Is Golden" was the first single from The Beths' 2022 album Expert in a Dying Field. Frontwoman Liz Stokes has said the song is about stress and anxiety manifesting as an intolerance to noise, with the guitars growing more fuzzed-out and chaotic as it builds; recording was interrupted by a four-month COVID lockdown, and the band finished the album during a three-day session in Los Angeles.

sigur ros|hljomalind.fact: "Hljomalind," from Sigur Ros's 2007 release Hvarf/Heim, is named after a Reykjavik record store once run by Kristinn "Kiddi Kanina" Saemundsson, the band's manager at the time. The song had actually been performed live since 1999 under earlier working titles, including "Rokklagid" ("The Rock Song") and "The Rabbit and the Prince."

bon iver|8 (circle).fact: "8 (circle)" is the fourth single from Bon Iver's 2016 album 22, A Million. Its lyric video features black-and-white artwork by Eric Timothy Carlson, who worked closely with the band throughout the recording sessions to create the visual identity for the whole album, where every track title includes a number.

nick cave & the bad seeds|long dark nigh.fact: "Long Dark Night" was released in July 2024 as a single from Nick Cave & the Bad Seeds' album Wild God. Cave has said the song draws on "Dark Night of the Soul," a 16th-century poem by the Spanish mystic St. John of the Cross, echoing its themes of struggle and transcendence.

chanel beads|song for the messenger.fact: "Song for the Messenger" is a single from Chanel Beads' sophomore album, Your Day Will Come, released via Jagjaguwar. The project is essentially the work of one musician, Shane Lavers, who builds his songs in a small Brooklyn studio by recording into whatever microphone happens to be nearby.

sunset rubdown|you go on ahead.fact: "You Go on Ahead" is a direct sequel to "Trumpet Trumpet, Toot Toot!" from Sunset Rubdown's earlier album Random Spirit Lover, the two songs forming songwriter Spencer Krug's two-part meditation on the contradictions of being a touring musician and performer.

frankie and the witch fingers|futurephob.fact: "Futurephobic" appears on Frankie and the Witch Fingers' 2023 album Data Doom. Its main riff was actually written years earlier during sessions for the band's previous record, Monsters Eating People Eating Monsters, then shelved until it resurfaced and fit the new album's vintage sci-fi concept; the band finished the track's overdubs while touring through France and Amsterdam.

the brook & the bluff|long limbs.fact: "Long Limbs," from The Brook & The Bluff's 2023 album Bluebeard, took about seven years to finish -- its chorus was originally written back in 2016. The title is also a nod to bandmate Joseph Settine's famously tall, lanky frame.

bad brains|sailin' on.fact: "Sailin' On" first appeared on Bad Brains' 1982 self-titled debut before being re-recorded for their 1983 follow-up, Rock for Light, which was produced by The Cars' Ric Ocasek.

model/actriz|doves.fact: "Doves" is a single from Model/Actriz's 2025 album Pirouette, which the band recorded across three studios -- Machines with Magnets in Pawtucket, Rhode Island, and The Cutting Room and Studio G in New York City -- with production by Seth Manchester. Much of the record was written while the band was on tour in 2023, and drummer Ruben Radlauer has said the techno and house music they were listening to on the road seeped into the album's sound.

modern baseball|apple cider, i don't min.fact: Modern Baseball split songwriting duties down the middle between co-frontmen Jake Ewald and Bren Lukens, and "Apple Cider, I Don't Mind" is one of Lukens's tracks from the band's 2016 album Holy Ghost. Critics noted it as a stylistic departure, an anthemic, post-rock-tinged song blending The Cure's atmospheric melodies with the widescreen guitar sound of U2's Joshua Tree era.

belle and sebastian|is it wicked not to.fact: "Is It Wicked Not to Care?" appears on Belle and Sebastian's 1998 album The Boy with the Arab Strap and marks the first time multi-instrumentalist Isobel Campbell sang lead vocals for the band. Frontman Stuart Murdoch wrote the song the morning after Scotland's win over Denmark in World Cup qualifying.

big red machine|hymnostic.fact: "Hymnostic" is the gospel-flavored highlight of Big Red Machine's 2018 self-titled debut, the collaborative project between Bon Iver's Justin Vernon and The National's Aaron Dessner. Dessner has said the song was designed as a communal singalong meant to invite as many voices as possible to join in, and Vernon noted it could work just as well arranged with fiddles and banjos.

panda bear|defense (feat. cindy lee).fact: "Defense" paired Panda Bear (Noah Lennox of Animal Collective) with Cindy Lee (Patrick Flegel) as the first single from Panda Bear's 2025 album Sinister Grift, his first solo LP in five years. The guitar-driven collaboration features Cindy Lee on guitar and was released October 15, 2024.

cap'n jazz|oh messy life.fact: "Oh Messy Life" is the second track on Cap'n Jazz's only full-length album, Shmap'n Shmazz, recorded over five days between December 27-31, 1994. The Chicago band broke up shortly after the record's 1995 release, but its chaotic, melodic style is now widely credited with helping push emo out of the punk underground and into indie rock.

lucy dacus|most wanted man.fact: "Most Wanted Man," from Lucy Dacus's 2025 album Forever Is a Feeling, is an upbeat love song dedicated to her boygenius bandmate Julien Baker, who also sings backing vocals on the track. The album was released March 28, 2025.

death cab for cutie|pep talk.fact: "Pep Talk" is track three on Death Cab for Cutie's 2025 album I Built You a Tower, the band's 11th studio album and first release on ANTI- Records after two decades on Atlantic. The record was produced by John Congleton and is the group's first full-length of new material since 2022's Asphalt Meadows.

caroline polachek|blood and butter.fact: "Blood and Butter," from Caroline Polachek's 2023 album Desire, I Want to Turn Into You, features a bagpipe solo by Scottish musician Brighde Chaimbeul, whom Polachek approached specifically to contribute to the Danny L. Harle co-produced track. Chaimbeul later joined Polachek onstage to perform the bagpipe break live.

strand of oaks|keys.fact: "Keys," from Strand of Oaks' 2019 album Eraserland, is a love song frontman Tim Showalter wrote for his wife Sue, built from real conversations the two had about growing older together. Showalter has said the second chorus captures the only take he and his producer could get through without getting emotional.

caribou|home.fact: Caribou's 2019 single "Home" is built around a sample of the song "Home" by Gloria Barnes, an obscure soul singer who released just one album, in 1971, before disappearing from the music industry. Dan Snaith found the track on YouTube and let the sample sit on his hard drive for over a year before finishing the song.

sharon van etten & the attachment theory.fact: "Afterlife" comes from the 2025 self-titled debut album by Sharon Van Etten & The Attachment Theory, the first time Van Etten released music as a true full band rather than as a solo artist with backing musicians.
