The song's video was Parks's third collaboration with director Molly Burdett, following "Black Dog" and "Hurt."

jungle|happy man.fact: "Happy Man" was released in May 2018 as a double single with "House in L.A." ahead of Jungle's second album, For Ever. The track later found a second life well beyond the album, turning up in an O2 phone commercial, Netflix's "Elite," and as the opening theme for Apple TV+'s "WeCrashed."

radiohead|paranoid android.fact: "Paranoid Android" was stitched together from three separate song fragments, each originally written by a different band member, in a process inspired by the multi-part structure of the Beatles' "Happiness Is a Warm Gun." Recorded at St Catherine's Court, a 15th-century mansion near Bath, the first edit ran over 14 minutes — including a long Jonny Greenwood organ interlude — before being trimmed to six and a half minutes for OK Computer.

hovvdy and runo plum|shooting star.fact: Released in February 2025, "Shooting Star" marked Hovvdy's first new song since their self-titled LP and paired the duo with Minnesota indie-folk artist runo plum, who had been opening dates on their tour. The result is an even softer, more lullaby-like track than typical Hovvdy fare.

nilufer yanya|in your head.fact: Released in January 2019 as the second single from her debut album Miss Universe, "In Your Head" was described by Nilufer Yanya as being about "the illusion of freedom" and how the mind can trap you in its own perceptions. Its video was filmed out in the desert near Las Vegas.

pixies|debaser.fact: Frank Black wrote "Debaser" after watching the 1929 surrealist short film Un Chien Andalou in a college film studies class, and coined the song's title himself — a "debaser," he explained, is "one who debases," and he wanted to introduce the word into the language. The chorus deliberately mixes languages, with Black singing the intentionally garbled phrase "un chien andalusia" simply because, in his words, "it sounds good."

jay som|the bus song.fact: Jay Som is the solo recording project of Melina Duterte, who wrote, recorded, and produced her 2017 debut album Everybody Works largely on her own. "The Bus Song," from that album, has been described as a glistening "mass-transit reverie" carrying echoes of sunshine pop.

the war on drugs|best night.fact: "Best Night" appears on The War on Drugs' 2011 album Slave Ambient and was later issued as its own single in 2012. Adam Granduciel wrote and co-produced the track with Jeff Zeigler, with onetime member Kurt Vile — who'd left the band a few years earlier to focus on his solo career — guesting on guitar.

spirit of the beehive|1/500.fact: "1/500" is a track from Spirit of the Beehive's 2024 album You'll Have to Lose Something, released on the Saddle Creek label. It was written by band members Zack Schwartz and Rivka Ravede, with additional performance from Corey Wichlin.

beck|cyanide breath mint.fact: "Cyanide Breath Mint" appears on Beck's stripped-down, lo-fi 1994 album One Foot in the Grave, recorded at Dub Narcotic Studio. Beck liked the phrase enough that he later named his own music publishing company, Cyanide Breathmint Music, after the song.

the last dinner party|sinner.fact: "Sinner" was the second single from The Last Dinner Party's debut album Prelude to Ecstasy, written by guitarist Lizzie Mayland and produced by James Ford. The album went on to debut at Number One on the UK Albums Chart, the biggest first-week showing for a debut band album in nine years.

wilco|random name generator.fact: "Random Name Generator" appears on Wilco's 2015 album Star Wars, which the band surprised fans by releasing as a free download with no advance notice. Critics noted the song's fuzzed-out riff and stomping drums channel the glam-rock swagger of T. Rex.

the national|alphabet city.fact: "Alphabet City" was released in August 2023 as one of two surprise new singles alongside "Space Invader," both arriving with visualizer videos directed by Pauline de Lassus (who records under the name Mina Tindle). "Space Invader" later resurfaced on the band's surprise second album that year, Laugh Track.

sufjan stevens|my rajneesh.fact: "My Rajneesh" was released in July 2020 as the B-side to a limited double-sided 12-inch vinyl single alongside "America," pressed to just 1,500 copies worldwide. Both tracks came from the same writing sessions that fed into Stevens's next album, The Ascension.

pure carrire|abracabruti.fact: "Abracabruti" comes from Pure Carriere's 2025 album Visions de l'enfer. The Quebec City act is a duo formed in 2017 by Jean-Michel Letendre-Veilleux and Laurence Gauthier-Brown, who also play in other local projects like Beat Sexu and Victime.

gelli haha|bounce house.fact: "Bounce House" was Gelli Haha's debut single, released in March 2025 and later included on her album Switcheroo. The track was produced by Sean Guerin, and its music video was filmed inside a colorful indoor playground.

savages|husbands.fact: "Husbands," from Savages' 2013 debut album Silence Yourself, borrows its title from a 1970 John Cassavetes film about three friends navigating a midlife crisis. Frontwoman Jehnny Beth said the song grew from a feeling that people today have become disconnected, "like smoke."

pavement|zurich is stained.fact: "Zurich Is Stained" comes from Pavement's 1992 debut album Slanted and Enchanted, recorded on a shoestring budget at drummer Gary Young's home studio over about ten days. It remains the only Pavement album to feature Young behind the kit.

local natives|past lives.fact: "Past Lives" was Local Natives' first new song in three years, arriving in 2016 as the lead single from their album Sunlit Youth following 2013's Hummingbird. Guitarist Taylor Rice said of the track, "The world is not static, it's made new over and over again."

sprints|rage.fact: "Rage" appears on All That Is Over, the 2025 sophomore album from Dublin band SPRINTS. Formed in 2019, the group is made up of Karla Chubb, Sam McCann, Jack Callan and Zac Stephenson, and the record was produced by Daniel Fox as a follow-up to their 2024 debut, Letter to Self.

yeah yeah yeahs|gold lion.fact: "Gold Lion," the lead single from Yeah Yeah Yeahs' 2006 album Show Your Bones, got its title from the two Gold Lion trophies won at the Cannes Lions advertising festival by an Adidas commercial that Karen O had sung on, composed by Sam "Squeak E. Clean" Spiegel and directed by Spike Jonze.

courting|pause at you (c u around).fact: "Pause At You" was released as the lead single from Courting's third album, Lust for Life, Or: How To Thread The Needle And Come Out The Other Side To Tell The Story, announced in late 2024 ahead of a March 2025 release.

weyes blood|children of the empire.fact: "Children of the Empire" is from Weyes Blood's 2022 album And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow, the second chapter in a trilogy that began with 2019's Titanic Rising. Natasha Mering said she realized she had "a few songs left over" from that earlier album, which grew into this one; she co-produced the track with Jonathan Rado.

bat for lashes|oh yeah.fact: "Oh Yeah" appears on Bat for Lashes' 2012 album The Haunted Man, written by Natasha Khan and produced by a team including Dan Carey, David Kosten, and Rob Ellis.

grizzly bear|three rings.fact: "Three Rings" was released as a single in May 2017 ahead of Grizzly Bear's album Painted Ruins. The track builds through layered vocal harmonies and woodwinds over a dusty electronic drum loop before a burst of guitar closes it out.

the fall|eat y'self fitter.fact: "Eat Y'self Fitter" opens The Fall's 1983 album Perverted by Language. Mark E. Smith built the song's chant-like chorus around ad slogans lifted from a Kellogg's All-Bran cereal campaign, and DJ John Peel later named it among his all-time favorite tracks.

the dandy warhols|i'd like to help you w.fact: This 2024 single comes from The Dandy Warhols' album Rockmaker and features a guitar solo from Slash. Frontman Courtney Taylor-Taylor described the track's sound as "real Vietnam-era acid rock," and the band has said they "just stared at each other with our mouths open" the first time they heard Slash's contributions played back in the studio.

hurray for the riff raff|pyramid scheme.fact: "Pyramid Scheme" was released February 20, 2025 as a standalone single, the band's first new music after their acclaimed 2024 album The Past Is Still Alive. The song channels contempt for the dark side of the internet and how it alienates and undermines artists and outsiders.

angelo de augustine|27.fact: "27" was released as a double single with "Hologram" in November 2022, Angelo De Augustine's first new music after his 2021 collaborative album with Sufjan Stevens, A Beginner's Mind. Stevens returned the favor here, contributing synthesizer, drum machine, electric guitar, bass, Fender Rhodes, and background vocals to the track.

st. vincent|marrow.fact: "Marrow" appears on St. Vincent's 2009 album Actor. Annie Clark has said the song grew out of her love of The Wizard of Oz, wanting to write about a character wishing "they had a spine made of iron," and aiming for a sound that was as visual and Technicolor as it was musical, built from distorted guitars, horns, and fluttering woodwinds.

mac demarco|gualala.fact: "Gualala" opens Mac DeMarco's 2023 all-instrumental album Five Easy Hot Dogs, a record where each track is named for a town he passed through on an actual road trip up the California and Canadian coast, with songs recorded and mixed at each stop. The album's only vocal moment anywhere is DeMarco's spoken count-in at the very start of this opening track.

darkside|s.n.c..fact: "S.N.C." comes from Darkside's 2025 album Nothing, the group's first LP since drummer Tlacael Esparza joined Nicolas Jaar and Dave Harrington as a full-time third member. The album was recorded across studios in Provence, Los Angeles, and Paris.

husker du|chartered trips.fact: "Chartered Trips" is track four on Husker Du's 1984 double album Zen Arcade, written and sung by Bob Mould with piano parts from both Mould and Grant Hart. It's frequently singled out as one of the album's more melodic, pop-oriented songs, one that pointed the way toward the band's next record, New Day Rising.

vacations|midwest.fact: "Midwest" appears on Australian band Vacations' 2023 album No Place Like Home. Singer Campbell Burns has said it was the first breakup song he'd ever written directly, inspired by the strain of leaving someone behind while out on tour, and he co-produced the track with John Velasquez.

belle and sebastian|unnecessary drama.fact: "Unnecessary Drama" was the lead single from Belle and Sebastian's 2022 album A Bit of Previous, the Scottish band's first full studio album since 2015. It was recorded in their hometown of Glasgow after the pandemic derailed original plans to record in Los Angeles, and its video shows the band comically working out their tensions with a therapist and team-building exercises.

alex g|southern sky.fact: "Southern Sky" appears on Alex G's 2019 album House of Sugar and features guest vocals from Emily Yacina. It arrived with an animated, black-and-white video from his longtime collaborator Elliott Bech, built around plunking keys, a running bassline, and impressionistic violin.

black midi|speedway.fact: "Speedway" was first released in January 2019 as a tour-only 12-inch before landing as track two on black midi's debut album Schlagenheim later that year. It marked one of bassist Cameron Picton's first lead-vocal turns for the band, giving the song a quieter, more subdued feel next to the record's noisier tracks.

julia holter|evening mood.fact: "Evening Mood," from Julia Holter's 2024 album Something in the Room She Moves, was partly inspired by her daughter's favorite film, Miyazaki's Ponyo. Holter wove an actual recording of her own pregnancy ultrasound heartbeat, run through a phaser, into the track alongside Dev Hoff's fretless bass and Chris Speed's clarinet.

destroyer|hydroplaning off the edge of t.fact: "Hydroplaning Off the Edge of the World" was the second single from Destroyer's 2025 album Dan's Boogie, the band's fourteenth studio record, produced by longtime collaborator John Collins. Across the album's nine songs, frontman Dan Bejar plays with characters like a lounge singer and a hustler.

youbet|carsick.fact: Youbet is a Brooklyn-based indie rock band fronted by Nick Llobet. "Carsick" was the first song they shared after signing to Hardly Art in late 2023, and it later appeared on the band's debut full-length, Way To Be.

alvvays|archie, marry me.fact: "Archie, Marry Me" is from Alvvays' self-titled 2014 debut album. Songwriter Molly Rankin has said she chose the name "Archie" because it was uncommon but felt right, writing the song from the perspective of poking fun at being in your twenties and surrounded by engaged friends.

fleet foxes|blue ridge mountains.fact: "Blue Ridge Mountains," written by frontman Robin Pecknold, appears on Fleet Foxes' self-titled 2008 debut album. It's a narrative song built around a missed connecting flight to the mountains near Asheville, North Carolina, layered over the band's harmony-heavy folk arrangements.

huron john|just me & friends.fact: "Just Me & Friends" was released as a 2023 single and later included on Huron John's third album, Indigo Jack & the New World Border (2024). Co-produced by Matt Neighbor, it blends neo-psychedelia with alt-pop and has been called "a love letter to honesty and pure connection."

bon iver|calgary.fact: "Calgary" was the first single from Bon Iver's self-titled second album (2011). Like much of the record, the song is named after a real place chosen mostly for its emotional resonance rather than literal geography — Justin Vernon has said he wrote about the Canadian city despite never having been there.

lucy dacus|hot and heavy.fact: "Hot & Heavy" opens Lucy Dacus's 2021 album Home Video and was its lead single. Dacus said she thought she was writing about an old friend but realized it was about outgrowing past versions of herself; the self-directed video was shot at Richmond's historic Byrd Theatre using home-video footage her dad took of her as a kid.

radiohead|bodysnatchers.fact: "Bodysnatchers," from 2007's In Rainbows, was recorded live with the full band playing together in one take — the only track on the album done that way. It was tracked at Tottenham House, a crumbling country mansion in Wiltshire where the band lived in caravans during sessions with producer Nigel Godrich.

the strokes|brooklyn bridge to chorus.fact: "Brooklyn Bridge to Chorus" was released April 6, 2020 as the third single from The Strokes' The New Abnormal, the band's first album produced by Rick Rubin. Its synth-driven, new-wave sound drew comparisons to Julian Casablancas's solo work with The Voidz.

beabadoobee|memories.fact: "Memories" comes from beabadoobee's 2026 album Pylon, released via Dirty Hit/Interscope. She co-wrote the acoustic-driven track with Shane Moran and Gianluca Buccellati and called it one of the happiest-sounding songs on the record, even though its lyrics dwell on the bittersweet pull of nostalgia.

the english beat|ranking full stop.fact: "Ranking Full Stop" was the lead single from The English Beat's 1980 debut I Just Can't Stop It. Its title borrows from Jamaican sound-system slang — "ranking" was a boastful term of respect used by toasting MCs, fitting since the band's own toaster performed under the stage name Ranking Roger.

julia jacklin|if i had the hand of god.fact: "If I Had the Hand of God" is a single from Julia Jacklin's 2026 album The Gem on 4AD. Jacklin wrote the country-rock track as a meditation on life as a touring musician, partly inspired by a recent trip to Nashville.

fontaines d.c.|cello song.fact: Fontaines D.C.'s cover of Nick Drake's 1969 "'Cello Song" (from Drake's Five Leaves Left) served as the lead single for the 2023 tribute album The Endless Coloured Ways – The Songs of Nick Drake. The band swapped Drake's cello-led acoustic arrangement for a driving backbeat and layered guitars, part of a 32-artist project that asked contributors to reinvent the songs rather than replicate them.

spoon|i summon you.fact: "I Summon You," from Spoon's 2005 album Gimme Fiction, was performed for the Black Cab Sessions series, whose motto is "one song, one take, one cab" — filming artists playing a single song while riding in the back of a moving London taxi. The band stripped the song down to just guitar and vocals for that version, versus the added bass and drums on the album cut.

gang of four|at home he's a tourist.fact: "At Home He's a Tourist," from Gang of Four's 1979 debut Entertainment!, peaked at No. 58 on the UK singles chart — still the highest chart position any Gang of Four single has reached. According to singer Jon King, guitarist Andy Gill recorded the song's jagged, scraping guitar part in a single take.

wild pink|cloud or mountain.fact: "Cloud or Mountain" appears on Wild Pink's 2024 album Dulling the Horns. The track shifts between a country-tinged feel and heavier, sludgier passages, and features pedal steel guitar from Mike "Slo-Mo" Brenner.

the mountain goats|get famous.fact: "Get Famous" is the horn-backed second track on The Mountain Goats' 2020 album Getting into Knives, recorded in a single week at Sam Phillips Recording in Memphis with producer Matt Ross-Spang and a crew of local session musicians. Its 2020 music video portrays the band members as bobblehead dolls.

modest mouse|interstate 8.fact: "Interstate 8" is the title track of Modest Mouse's second EP, released on Up Records in 1996. It was produced by Steve Wold and recorded at Moon Music in Olympia, Washington, bridging the gap between the band's debut album and 1997's The Lonesome Crowded West.

vampire weekend|don't lie.fact: "Don't Lie" appears on Vampire Weekend's 2013 album Modern Vampires of the City. Frontman Ezra Koenig has described it as a kind of sequel to the band's earlier songs "M79" and "White Sky," built around a simpler, more direct arrangement than listeners might expect from the band.

sigur ros|starálfur.fact: "Starálfur," meaning "staring elf," appears on Sigur Rós's 1999 album Ágætis byrjun. Sung in Icelandic by Jónsi, the lyrics describe going to bed after a long day in blue pajamas and suddenly noticing the mythical staring elf gazing back from the room.

bully|i remember.fact: "I Remember" was the first single from Bully's 2015 debut album Feels Like. The sub-two-minute punk track was written and sung by frontwoman Alicia Bognanno, who also produced and mixed the recording herself.

massive attack|unfinished sympathy.fact: For "Unfinished Sympathy," from 1991's Blue Lines, producer Johnny Dollar brought in arranger Wil Malone to record a 40-piece orchestra at Abbey Road Studios. The orchestral session cost so much that Massive Attack had to sell one of their vehicles, a Mitsubishi Shogun, to help cover the bill.

adrianne lenker|cradle.fact: "cradle" was the first single from Adrianne Lenker's 2018 solo album abysskiss. She recorded the album with Luke Temple of Here We Go Magic at Panoramic House in West Marin, California, shortly after two weeks spent traveling through the American South.

car seat headrest|nervous young inhumans.fact: "Nervous Young Inhumans" appears on Car Seat Headrest's Twin Fantasy (Face to Face). Songwriter Will Toledo has said the title nods to "galvanism," the long-obsolete scientific theory — made famous through Mary Shelley's Frankenstein — that electricity flowing through the bloodstream powers life. He used that idea as a lens for writing about creating and inhabiting characters in his songs.

wilco|box full of letters.fact: "Box Full of Letters" was Wilco's debut single, released from their first album A.M. in 1995. It's often read as addressing the breakup of Jeff Tweedy's previous band, Uncle Tupelo, with its multilayered guitars giving the track a gritty, lived-in texture.

yo la tengo|wasn't born to follow.fact: Yo La Tengo's version of "Wasn't Born to Follow" is a cover of the Byrds' 1968 track, originally written by Gerry Goffin and Carole King, released on the band's Sleepless Night EP via Matador. Longtime collaborator Dave Schramm plays lead guitar on the cover, which stays close to the folk-rock feel of the original.

spacemen 3|losing touch with my mind.fact: "Losing Touch With My Mind" opens Spacemen 3's 1986 debut album Sound of Confusion. It's built from a cycling wave of guitar feedback that gradually gets wrestled back into driving, classic garage-rock rhythm, setting the tone for the band's recorded career.

andrew bird|imitosis.fact: "Imitosis" started life as a slower, sparser song called "I" (performed live as "Capital I") on Andrew Bird's 2003 album Weather Systems. He reworked it into the more upbeat "Imitosis" for his 2007 album Armchair Apocrypha.

destroyer|bologna (feat. fiver).fact: "Bologna" features Simone Schmidt of the band Fiver on co-lead vocals, and Dan Bejar has said it's the first Destroyer song where he cast himself as a supporting character while Schmidt's part drives the narrative. It's the lead single from Destroyer's 2025 album Dan's Boogie, with a video directed by David Galloway starring Bejar and Schmidt.

big thief|masterpiece.fact: "Masterpiece" is the title track of Big Thief's debut studio album, released May 27, 2016 on Saddle Creek Records. NPR's Bob Boilen singled it out as one of the best songs he'd heard that year.

siouxsie and the banshees|she's a carniv.fact: "She's a Carnival" is track four on Siouxsie and the Banshees' 1982 album A Kiss in the Dreamhouse, with Steven Severin on bass, John McGeoch on guitar, and Budgie on drums. Critics have described it as a gutsy, organ-driven rocker that lives up to its title.

woods|little black flowers.fact: "Little Black Flowers" was released August 30, 2023 as a double single with "Day Moving On" ahead of Woods' album Perennial. It was recorded with longtime producer Jarvis Taveniere at Panoramic House in Stinson Beach, California, with additional sessions in Los Angeles and Stone Ridge, New York.

handsome furs|legal tender.fact: "Legal Tender" is the opening track on Handsome Furs' 2009 album Face Control, written by the duo of Dan Boeckner and Alexei Perry. It was recorded and mixed by Arlen Thompson at Mount Zoomer studio and mastered by Harris Newman at Hotel2Tango.

waxahatchee|oxbow.fact: "Oxbow" is the opening track on Waxahatchee's 2020 album Saint Cloud, which marked a turn toward a warmer, more rootsy Americana sound for songwriter Katie Crutchfield compared to her earlier, more lo-fi records.

japanese breakfast|orlando in love.fact: "Orlando in Love" was released January 7, 2025 as the lead single announcing Japanese Breakfast's album For Melancholy Brunettes (& Sad Women), written by Michelle Zauner and produced by Blake Mills. The title nods to Orlando Innamorato, the unfinished Renaissance-era epic poem by Matteo Maria Boiardo.

the smiths|barbarism begins at home.fact: On "Barbarism Begins at Home," from 1985's Meat Is Murder, drummer Mike Joyce cued his part off Andy Rourke's repetitive, funk-inspired bass line rather than Johnny Marr's guitar — a rare arrangement choice in the Smiths' catalog. Marr later praised Rourke's bass work on the track as a highlight of the record.

xtc|senses working overtime.fact: "Senses Working Overtime," the lead single from XTC's 1982 album English Settlement, became the band's highest-charting UK single at number 10, while the album itself reached number 5 — the commercial peak of XTC's career.

beach house|myth.fact: "Myth" is the opening track and lead single from Beach House's 2012 album Bloom, released via Sub Pop. Critics called its organ-and-synth-driven intro a "monumental kick-off" to the record.

sparks|falling in love with myself again.fact: "Falling in Love with Myself Again" appears on Sparks' 1974 breakthrough album Kimono My House, written by Ron Mael and produced by Muff Winwood — former bassist of the Spencer Davis Group turned in-house producer for Island Records.

talking heads|slippery people.fact: "Slippery People," from Talking Heads' 1983 album Speaking in Tongues, blends gospel, funk and reggae, with lyrics nodding to the Book of Ezekiel's "four living creatures" and "wheel in the middle of a wheel." Gospel singer Mavis Staples was drawn to the song and has kept it in her live repertoire ever since.

weyes blood|it's not just me, it's every.fact: "It's Not Just Me, It's Everybody" is the lead single from Weyes Blood's 2022 album And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow, co-written with Ben Babbitt and Jonathan Rado and featuring harpist Mary Lattimore. Weyes Blood has called it a "Buddhist anthem" about the shared, universal nature of personal pain.

frankie cosmos|on the lips.fact: "On the Lips" originally appeared on Greta Kline's 2013 self-released collection im sorry im hi lets go. She rerecorded it and issued it as a single in March 2016 ahead of her second studio album, Next Thing.

iron and wine|lovesong of the buzzard.fact: "Lovesong of the Buzzard" is track three on Iron & Wine's 2007 album The Shepherd's Dog, Sam Beam's first album recorded with a full backing band rather than largely solo at home.

amber arcades|fading lines.fact: "Fading Lines" is the title track and second single from Amber Arcades' 2016 debut album. Songwriter Annelotte de Graaf has said it was loosely inspired by her grandfather's death and the way memories blur together over time; its music video features a parachutist falling in reverse.

the national|day i die.fact: "Day I Die" was released August 29, 2017 as the fourth single from The National's seventh album, Sleep Well Beast, following "The System Only Dreams in Total Darkness," "Guilty Party," and "Carin at the Liquor Store."

sleater-kinney|all hands on the bad one.fact: "All Hands on the Bad One" is the title track (and third song) from Sleater-Kinney's fifth album, released May 2, 2000 on Kill Rock Stars. The record was produced by John Goodmanson at Jackpot! Studio and later earned a GLAAD Media Award nomination for Outstanding Music Album.

mitski|my body's made of crushed little.fact: "My Body's Made of Crushed Little Stars" is track seven on Mitski's 2016 album Puberty 2, written and recorded with longtime producer Patrick Hyland at Acme Studios in New York. At under two minutes, the folk-punk track has remained a staple of her live setlists, including her Be the Cowboy tour.

neko case|fox confessor brings the flood.fact: "Fox Confessor Brings the Flood" is the sixth track and title song of Neko Case's fourth solo album, released March 7, 2006 on ANTI- Records. The album is known for its fable-like, myth-infused imagery and remains one of her most acclaimed releases.

@|punish my mind.fact: "Punish My Mind" comes from @ (the art-rock duo also rendered "At")'s 4AD debut album Autosmile. The band has said it's one of the oldest recordings they made for the record, built around a horn arrangement and layered vocal harmonies. The finished mix even weaves in the sampled screech of a monkey.

fiona apple|werewolf.fact: "Werewolf" appears on Fiona Apple's 2012 album The Idler Wheel Is Wiser Than the Driver of the Screw and Whipping Cords Will Serve You More Than Ropes Will Ever Do. Apple has described it as a song about realizing you can still choose to stay friends with someone from a past relationship even after things didn't work out. The arrangement starts out spare before growing more complex, and the track closes with the sound of children playing.

stiff little fingers|suspect device.fact: "Suspect Device" was Stiff Little Fingers' debut single, recorded on 4 February 1978 in a Downtown Radio studio in Newtownards normally used for recording jingles. Belfast journalist Gordon Ogilvie wrote the lyrics and handed them to singer Jake Burns after the band's fourth-ever gig. The band released it themselves on their own Rigid Digits label, and after a copy reached John Peel, who played it repeatedly on air, Rough Trade signed on to distribute it, helping it sell over 30,000 copies.

wednesday|quarry.fact: "Quarry" appears on Wednesday's 2023 album Rat Saw God, which the Asheville, North Carolina band recorded in just a week at the local Drop of Sun studio. Several reviewers noted that the song's opening verse echoes the chord changes and mood of The Kinks' "Waterloo Sunset" before the chorus breaks into a wall of distorted, shoegaze-indebted guitar.

sufjan stevens|flint (for the unemployed.fact: "Flint (For the Unemployed and Underpaid)" opens Sufjan Stevens' 2003 album Michigan, the first entry in his planned "50 states" project. The track begins with a spare, minimal piano line that carries most of the song, and an electric guitar only enters as a surprise about three minutes in to close things out. Stevens wrote, performed, and recorded nearly the entire album himself while working a day job in New York.

bauhaus|kick in the eye.fact: "Kick in the Eye" was released as a single in March 1981 ahead of Bauhaus's second album, Mask, which expanded the band's sound with saxophone, keyboards, and funk-inflected rhythms. The song's title was drawn from a line in Jack Kerouac's novel Satori in Paris. It became one of two singles from Mask to crack the UK Top 60 that year.

the white stripes|ball and biscuit.fact: At 7:17, "Ball and Biscuit" is the longest studio track The White Stripes ever recorded, and Jack White wrote it on the spot while making 2003's Elephant. It was recorded live to an 8-track reel-to-reel machine at Toe Rag Studios in London, a strictly analog session where the band famously used no computers at any stage of recording, mixing, or mastering. The song's heavily distorted guitar solos, run through an octave pedal, were improvised.

king gizzard and the lizard wizard|big f.fact: "Big Fig Wasp" is the second track on King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's 2016 album Nonagon Infinity, a record built so its songs flow in an endless loop. While most of the album was tracked at Daptone Records in Brooklyn, "Big Fig Wasp" was recorded separately at a different studio back home in Melbourne, with Paul Maybury engineering and Michael Badger handling vocals.

aphex twin|ageispolis.fact: "Ageispolis" is the fourth track on Aphex Twin's 1992 debut Selected Ambient Works 85-92, clocking in at 5:23. The album compiles ambient and techno pieces Richard D. James made on cassette dating back to when he was just 13 or 14 years old. Released on Apollo, a subsidiary of Belgian label R&S Records, it's now regarded as a defining, genre-expanding work of ambient electronic music.

elliott smith|coming up roses.fact: "Coming Up Roses" is the sixth track on Elliott Smith's self-titled 1995 album, running 3:10. It got its own music video that year, directed by Ross Harris. The self-titled record built on Smith's debut Roman Candles and cemented his reputation for stark, intimate songwriting.

father john misty|funny girl.fact: "Funny Girl" was the lead single off Father John Misty's 2022 album Chloë and the Next 20th Century, released in January of that year with a music video directed by Nicholas Ashe Bateman. Musically it's a string-laden, swing-era throwback that tells the story of a rising Hollywood starlet. The album was recorded at Jonathan Wilson's Five Star Studios with additional strings, brass, and woodwinds tracked at United Recordings.

toro y moi|sidelines.fact: "Sidelines" is the second track on Toro y Moi's surprise 2023 EP Sandhills, a tribute to Chaz Bear's hometown of Columbia, South Carolina. The song opens with the narrator recalling being a third-string player on a Friday night football team, using that memory as a jumping-off point for a broader look back at growing up. The EP runs just 13 minutes across five songs.

wild nothing|life of pause.fact: "Life of Pause" is the title track of Wild Nothing's 2016 album, released on Captured Tracks and Bella Union and produced by Thom Monahan. The song's shimmering synths and driving drums have drawn comparisons to early-1980s David Bowie, and critics singled it out as one of the record's most purely pop moments.

wipers|youth of america.fact: The title track of Wipers' 1981 album Youth of America stretches to roughly ten minutes, a deliberate response from frontman Greg Sage against the era's trend of short, fast punk songs. The sprawling, motorik track went on to influence Sonic Youth and the broader noise-rock scene, and it's been covered by both the Melvins and Mission of Burma. Kurt Cobain later named the Youth of America album among his fifty favorite albums of all time.

radiohead|i might be wrong.fact: The version of "I Might Be Wrong" many fans know best is actually a live recording, released on Radiohead's 2001 live album I Might Be Wrong: Live Recordings. Captured during the band's Kid A and Amnesiac-era tour, the live arrangement leans harder into the rhythm section than the more atmospheric studio version from Amnesiac, giving it a rawer, more rock-driven feel.

alabama shakes|gimme all your love.fact: "Gimme All Your Love," written by Brittany Howard for Alabama Shakes' 2015 album Sound & Color, builds its drama around a midsong tempo shift and vocal effects on Howard's voice. After debuting it on Saturday Night Live, the band later played the song live at Prince's Paisley Park studio in Minneapolis in June 2015, with Prince himself joining them onstage for an extended guitar solo.

animal collective|grass.fact: "Grass" was released as a single off Animal Collective's 2005 album Feels. For the whole record, the band tuned their guitars to match a friend's piano, which happened to already be out of tune, giving the album -- and "Grass" in particular -- its distinctively warped, chiming guitar tone.

wolf parade|dinner bells.fact: "Dinner Bells," written by Spencer Krug, closes out Wolf Parade's 2005 debut album Apologies to the Queen Mary at over seven minutes long. An earlier, shorter version of the song had already appeared on the band's self-released 2003 EP before this fuller studio take. Modest Mouse's Isaac Brock produced most of the album, which was recorded between Portland, Oregon, and Montreal.

tame impala|yes i'm changing.fact: "Yes I'm Changing" is the third track on Tame Impala's 2015 album Currents, a record built entirely around the theme of personal transformation. As with nearly everything on Currents, Kevin Parker wrote, played, produced, and engineered the song by himself. Parker later said the songwriting came together so quickly it felt like someone else had written it.

new order|the perfect kiss.fact: The music video for New Order's "The Perfect Kiss" was directed by filmmaker Jonathan Demme and simply shows the band performing the entire nearly 11-minute song live in their practice room. The band played live rather than miming, recording straight to 24-track tape, and the shoot was filmed by cinematographer Henri Alekan, who decades earlier had shot Jean Cocteau's Beauty and the Beast.

hatchie|sure.fact: "Sure" is the second single from Hatchie's debut EP Sugar & Spice (2018), the breakthrough release that introduced Australian dream-pop songwriter Harriette Pilbeam to a wider audience. In February 2018 the track was remixed by Robin Guthrie, guitarist of dream-pop pioneers Cocteau Twins, a fitting nod given the genre's influence on Hatchie's sound. The EP was released through Double Double Whammy, Ivy League, and Heavenly Recordings.

black belt eagle scout|indians never die.fact: "Indians Never Die" is a track from Mother of My Children, the debut album by Black Belt Eagle Scout, the project of musician Katherine Paul, who grew up on the Swinomish Reservation in Washington state and is Swinomish and Inupiaq. The album was first self-released in August 2017 through Good Cheer Records before being reissued by Saddle Creek Records in September 2018, introducing Paul's music to a much wider national audience.

wire|too late.fact: "Too Late" appears on Wire's second album, Chairs Missing, released in September 1978. Produced by Mike Thorne, the record pushed the English post-punk band toward more atmospheric, synth-tinged textures than their stripped-down 1977 debut, Pink Flag, and the track was written by guitarist Bruce Gilbert.

jungle|heavy, california.fact: "Heavy, California" is actually from Jungle's second album, For Ever, released in September 2018 on XL Recordings, rather than the band's self-titled 2014 debut, which had been shortlisted for the Mercury Prize. The track was shared as a single in July 2018, one of the first tastes of the follow-up record.

sault|why why why why why.fact: "Why Why Why Why Why" is track four on 5, the 2019 album by the anonymous UK collective SAULT, released through Forever Living Originals. SAULT built its reputation by releasing music with almost no promotional interviews or photos, letting records like 5 speak for themselves.

wilco|casino queen.fact: "Casino Queen" is a highlight from Wilco's 1995 debut album, A.M., named after a real riverboat casino. Jeff Tweedy has said he wrote the song at his father's suggestion that the boat would make good song material, and former Uncle Tupelo touring guitarist Brian Henneman guests on the track's raucous slide guitar.

arlo parks|softly.fact: "Softly," released in February 2022, was Arlo Parks' first new single following her acclaimed 2021 debut album, Collapsed in Sunbeams. She co-wrote the track with veteran producer Paul Epworth, pairing its bright, upbeat-sounding production with lyrics about the fragile, bittersweet final days of a relationship.

the cure|boys don't cry.fact: "Boys Don't Cry" was first released as a standalone UK single in June 1979 and, despite later becoming one of The Cure's most beloved songs, failed to crack the UK top 75 at the time. It became the title track of the American compilation album Boys Don't Cry, issued in February 1980, and was written by founding members Michael Dempsey, Robert Smith, and Lol Tolhurst.

dinosaur jr.|watch the corners.fact: "Watch the Corners" was released as the lead single from Dinosaur Jr.'s tenth studio album, I Bet on Sky, which came out in September 2012. The band gave the track away as a free download alongside its music video to introduce fans to the record ahead of release.

soccer mommy|abigail.fact: "Abigail," a single from Soccer Mommy's 2024 album Evergreen, is a sincere serenade to Abigail, a non-playable villager character from the farming video game Stardew Valley. Sophie Allison originally wrote it as a casual songwriting exercise but liked the result enough to include it on the finished record.

andrew bird|roma fade.fact: "Roma Fade" was released as a single in March 2016 ahead of Andrew Bird's album Are You Serious, where it appears as the second track. The song opens with one of Bird's signature whistled melodies before building into full-band instrumentation, and the album overall features guest contributions from Fiona Apple and Blake Mills.

siouxsie and the banshees|kiss them for.fact: "Kiss Them for Me" became Siouxsie and the Banshees' biggest American hit, reaching number 23 on the Billboard Hot 100 after its 1991 release from the album Superstition. Its title borrows from the 1957 film Kiss Them for Me, which starred Jayne Mansfield and Cary Grant, and the lyrics work in Mansfield's real-life catchphrase "divoon."

destroyer|kaputt.fact: The title track of Destroyer's 2011 breakout album Kaputt, written by Dan Bejar, name-checks a run of real British music magazines in its lyrics -- "Sounds, Smash Hits, Melody Maker, NME" -- as part of its hazy, sophisti-pop meditation on the music press. The Merge Records album became the project's most critically celebrated release to date.

pixies|wave of mutilation.fact: Beyond the familiar version on 1989's Doolittle, the Pixies recorded an entirely different, slower arrangement of "Wave of Mutilation" known as the "UK Surf" version, originally released as a B-side to the "Here Comes Your Man" single. The song's title was later reused for Wave of Mutilation: Best of Pixies, a 2004 career-spanning compilation.

black midi|sugar/tzu.fact: "Sugar/Tzu" is a single from black midi's second album, Hellfire (2022), telling a speculative story of two 600-pound boxers fighting in a fictional "Leadweight" division in the year 2163. Its music video, directed by Noel Paul, won Best Cinematography in a Video at the 2022 UK Music Video Awards.

khruangbin|camo me quieres.fact: The song, properly titled "Como Me Quieres," comes from Khruangbin's 2018 album Con Todo el Mundo. Bassist Laura Lee based it on a running exchange with her grandfather, who would ask her "Como me quieres?" ("How do you love me?") and only accept one answer -- "Con todo el mundo" ("With all the world") -- which also became the album's title.

band of horses|the general specific.fact: "The General Specific" actually comes from Band of Horses' second album, Cease to Begin, released on Sub Pop in October 2007, rather than the band's later album Infinite Arms. It sits as track five on that record, a lo-fi, foot-stomping pop tune that showcases frontman Ben Bridwell's gentler melodic side.

westside cowboy|don't throw rocks.fact: "Don't Throw Rocks" is the lead single from Westside Cowboy's second EP, So Much Country 'Till We Get There, released in January 2026 by the Manchester four-piece, winners of the 2025 Glastonbury Emerging Talent Competition. The song grew out of a lo-fi drum-machine demo made in a bandmate's bedroom and reflects on the passing of time.

bat for lashes|glass.fact: "Glass" is actually the opening track of Bat for Lashes' second album, Two Suns, released in April 2009, rather than her 2006 debut Fur and Gold. The sweeping opener sets the tone for a record built around Natasha Khan's self-created alter ego, Pearl, a device she used to explore themes of duality throughout the album.

anna burch|2 cool 2 care.fact: "2 Cool 2 Care" opens Anna Burch's debut solo album, Quit the Curse, released in February 2018. The record grew out of Burch's scrappy phone demos, which Chicago musician Paul Cherry helped flesh out into full band arrangements.

beach house|10 mile stereo.fact: "10 Mile Stereo" was recorded in July 2009 at Dreamland Studio in Hurley, New York, for Beach House's breakthrough third album, Teen Dream (2010). The shoegaze-leaning track built a devoted following of its own, selling over 40,000 digital downloads by 2012, the biggest-selling individual track from the album at that point.

eels|i like birds.fact: "I Like Birds" appears on Eels' 2001 album Souljacker, released on DreamWorks Records. The track pairs close-harmony backing vocals and a chirpy whistled hook with grumbling lyrics about "mean little people," a wry contrast that makes it one of the record's most purely buoyant, playful moments despite frontman E's often downbeat songwriting reputation.

julien baker and torres|sugar in the tan.fact: "Sugar in the Tank" is the debut single from the duo Julien Baker & TORRES, released on Matador Records and premiered live on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. It later opened the pair's debut album together, Send a Prayer My Way (April 18, 2025), a record built around their shared love of classic country songwriting and imagery.

the war on drugs|red eyes.fact: "Red Eyes" was released as the lead single from The War on Drugs' Lost in the Dream on December 4, 2013, roughly three months ahead of the full album. Frontman Adam Granduciel spent about 15 months writing, demoing, and recording the record across five different studios in several states, an unusually drawn-out process for the band.

iron and wine|such great heights.fact: Iron & Wine's hushed acoustic cover of The Postal Service's electronic track "Such Great Heights" strips the song down to just Sam Beam's fingerpicked guitar and whispery vocal. The cover reached a huge audience after being featured in the 2004 film Garden State and its soundtrack, and later turned up in ad campaigns for M&M's and Ask.com.

weyes blood|wild time.fact: "Wild Time," from Weyes Blood's 2019 album Titanic Rising, builds from Natalie Mering's piano and acoustic guitar into a lush orchestral arrangement featuring strings, trumpet, and a full-throated French horn solo. The dense, cinematic orchestration — with contributions from players like Daphne Chen and Eric Gorfain — reflects the album's broader 1970s-FM-radio-inspired production style.

beck|hotwax.fact: "Hotwax" is track two on Beck's 1996 album Odelay, co-produced with the Dust Brothers (credited on the song as E.Z. Mike and King Gizmo alongside Beck). The track layers Beck's own harmonica playing and turntable scratching over a loose breakbeat, a grab-bag collage approach typical of the album's dense, sample-heavy sound.

boygenius|souvenir.fact: "Souvenir" closes out boygenius's self-titled 2018 EP on Matador Records, the trio's first release together. Julien Baker, Phoebe Bridgers, and Lucy Dacus each take their own verse on the hushed, acoustic track, and a lyric from the song — "twenty dollars and a souvenir" — resurfaces years later in "$20," a track on the group's 2023 full-length, the record.

beirut|nantes.fact: "Nantes," from Beirut's 2006 debut Gulag Orkestar, was partly inspired by Jamaican dub producer King Tubby's reggae records; Zach Condon has joked about the connection, and the band reportedly plays the song as a straight reggae tune at soundchecks, just never during an actual show. Condon recorded the whole album as a teenager in his bedroom in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

alex g|mis.fact: "Mis" is track six on Alex G's self-released 2012 album Rules, which he recorded and produced entirely on his own and put out independently via Bandcamp — the cover art was even painted by his mother. The lo-fi record predates Alex G's wider breakthrough and was later remastered and reissued on vinyl and CD by Lucky Number in 2015.

vampire weekend|bambina.fact: "Bambina," from Vampire Weekend's 2024 album Only God Was Above Us, riffs on François Couperin's 1717 harpsichord piece "Les Barricades Mystérieuses" — an unusual reference for a rock band, but one that fits the Baroque influences that have run through Vampire Weekend's music since their earliest records.

the apples in stereo|tidal wave.fact: "Tidal Wave" was the title track of the band's debut 7" EP, self-released in June 1993 under the name the Apples (before they became the Apples in Stereo) — notably, it was also the very first official release on the influential Elephant 6 Recording Co. label. Leader Robert Schneider co-wrote the song with Chris Parfitt and produced the whole EP on a four-track recorder.

angel olsen|acrobat.fact: "Acrobat" opens Angel Olsen's 2012 debut full-length, Half Way Home, released on the small label Bathetic Records. The track is built around gentle acoustic guitar layered with a droning pump organ, a spare, lo-fi arrangement characteristic of Olsen's early era before her later, more fully produced band records.

frankie rose|best of times.fact: "Best of Times" is the eighth track on Frankie Rose's 2026 album Hila, her sixth solo record and first in three years, made after she toured with The Jesus and Mary Chain in 2024. The song's flowing saxophone part, played by Jeff Tobias, gives it an '80s, cinematic feel that reviewers compared to a Michael Mann film score.

mission of burma|forget.fact: "Forget" appears as a bonus track on CD reissues of Mission of Burma's 1982 debut album, Vs. The band later reused the title for Forget, a 1988 compilation on Taang! Records gathering demos and outtakes the group recorded between 1979 and 1982, offering an early look at the band's pre-Vs. sound.

this is lorelei|holo boy.fact: "Holo Boy" is the closing title track of This Is Lorelei's December 2025 album, which collects re-recorded versions of songs Nate Amos originally released across nine different Bandcamp projects between 2014 and 2021. Amos says the roughly 90-second lo-fi track was written in Chicago around 2014-2015, making it the oldest song on the record and one of his personal favorites.

king gizzard and the lizard wizard|atara.fact: "Ataraxia," from King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's 2021 microtonal album L.W., is the only song on the record with a sole songwriting credit, as guitarist Joey Walker wrote, sang, and mixed it himself. To keep the parts from clashing, the track pairs guitar in the A Subminor Phrygian scale with vocals kept in the standard 12-equal A Mixolydian scale, while bandmate Stu Mackenzie adds sitar and pungi.

the clash|should i stay or should i go.fact: Mick Jones wrote "Should I Stay or Should I Go" (from 1982's Combat Rock) about his on-and-off relationship with singer Ellen Foley, though he later said the song "wasn't about anything specific" and was really just the band's attempt at writing a classic rock song. The Clash had famously racked up hit singles without ever cracking the UK Top Ten — until the song soundtracked a 1991 Levi's commercial and was rereleased, finally giving the band their only UK number-one single.

the beths|out of sight.fact: "Out of Sight" is the third single from The Beths' 2020 album Jump Rope Gazers, with a music video that shows the band going bird watching, shot on Super 8 film and mixed with archival bird footage. Singer Elizabeth Stokes said the band deliberately played the song "more fragile" than they usually allow themselves to be, highlighting bassist Benjamin Sinclair's melodic playing.

elliott smith|pictures of me.fact: "Pictures of Me" is track five on Elliott Smith's 1997 album Either/Or. Like his earlier records, it was recorded in various apartments around his adopted hometown of Portland, Oregon, with Smith playing every instrument himself, and the album was produced by Smith along with Tom Rothrock and Rob Schnapf. An unreleased live recording of the song from a July 1997 YoYo A Go Go festival performance later appeared on the album's 20th-anniversary expanded edition in 2017.

future islands|cave.fact: "Cave" is a track from Future Islands' fifth studio album, The Far Field, released on April 7, 2017 — not from their earlier breakthrough record Singles, as is sometimes assumed. The band supported the album with a notable touring run following their star-making 2014 Letterman performance of a different song, "Seasons (Waiting on You)."

unknown mortal orchestra|how can you luv.fact: "How Can You Luv Me" appears on Unknown Mortal Orchestra's self-titled debut album, released June 21, 2011. The track was produced by frontman Ruban Nielson and incorporates a sample of "151 Rome Proof" by Lee Taylor & Soul Twisters Ltd. The debut album went on to win the 2012 Taite Music Prize in the band's native New Zealand.

spoon|you got yr. cherry bomb.fact: "You Got Yr. Cherry Bomb" is the third track on Spoon's sixth studio album, Ga Ga Ga Ga Ga, released July 10, 2007 on Merge Records and Anti- (it's sometimes mixed up with the earlier Kill the Moonlight, but it's a different record). The album clocks in at just over 36 minutes across ten tracks.

bon iver|imi.fact: "iMi" began as an idea Justin Vernon worked on with engineer Josh Berg at his April Base studio in Wisconsin. Minnesota musician Bobby Raps and producer Wheezy (known for his work with Young Thug and Future) contributed drum programming before Vernon finished the track at Sonic Ranch studio in Texas. It appears on Bon Iver's 2019 album i,i.

stef chura|the concrete.fact: "The Concrete" is the title track of Stef Chura's 2026 album Dancing Alone on the Concrete, her first LP in seven years. It was recorded at Chase Park Transduction studio in Athens, Georgia, produced by Robert Schneider of the Apples in Stereo, and features guest contributions from R.E.M.'s Peter Buck and Mike Mills alongside Sugar's David Barbe.

big thief|real love.fact: "Real Love" appears on Big Thief's debut album, Masterpiece, released May 27, 2016 on Saddle Creek Records (not on the later Capacity, as is sometimes assumed). It was released as a single on March 17, 2016, making it one of the first songs the band ever put out.

freak slug|muse.fact: "Muse" closes out Amulet, the second album by Freak Slug — the project of Manchester, UK singer-songwriter and visual artist Xenya Genovese — released September 18, 2026. It follows her 2024 debut album I Blow Out Big Candles and marks a sonic evolution for the project, which draws comparisons to Elliott Smith's intimate, double-tracked vocal style.

radiohead|identikit.fact: Radiohead debuted "Identikit" live at the American Airlines Arena in Miami on February 27, 2012, years before it had an official studio release. The band later tracked a version at Jack White's Third Man Records studio during a tour stop, though those recordings were ultimately scrapped; the song finally surfaced in finished form on 2016's A Moon Shaped Pool.

sonic youth|100%.fact: The music video for Sonic Youth's "100%," the lead single from 1992's Dirty, was directed by Tamra Davis and Spike Jonze and shot around Los Angeles, with Jonze filming much of it from a skateboard. It features then-skateboarder (later actor) Jason Lee, and bassist Kim Gordon plays a yellow Fender bass borrowed from actor Keanu Reeves. The song became Sonic Youth's highest-charting single to that point, reaching No. 4 on Billboard's Alternative Airplay chart.

phoebe bridgers|on video.fact: "On Video" was written by Phoebe Bridgers for the end credits of the 2026 A24 thriller Primetime, starring Robert Pattinson. She co-wrote it with Jack Antonoff and Christian Lee Hutson, with production handled by Antonoff, Ethan Gruska, and Marshall Vore, and has since added it to her live setlist on tour.

ween|gabrielle.fact: "Gabrielle" was originally recorded by Ween in 1994 during the sessions for their album Chocolate and Cheese but was left off that record. It finally saw official release more than a decade later on the 2005 outtakes compilation Shinola, Vol. 1.

young jesus|brenda and diane.fact: "Brenda & Diane" is a single from Young Jesus's album The Fool on Saddle Creek Records. Songwriter John Rossiter based the Springsteen-indebted rocker on a real encounter with two older women who humbled the narrator out of his own sense of superiority and judgment by showing him the fuller, more complex life they were actually living.

@|bird.fact: "Bird" is a single by the Philadelphia art-folk duo @ (Victoria Rose and Stone Filipczak), taken from their debut album Autosmile on 4AD. The duo says the song was inspired by dead birds that kept turning up on their deck and was written during a bike ride through Druid Hill Park in Baltimore; the lyrics lean on puns to lighten the subject matter.

strand of oaks|heal.fact: "Heal" is the title track of Strand of Oaks' 2014 album, which marked a dramatic stylistic turn for songwriter Timothy Showalter — away from his earlier folk-rooted Americana sound and into a heavier, '70s/'80s/'90s-inspired hard-rock style. The record was produced by John Congleton with engineer/synth player Ben Vehorn and drummer Steve Clements, and it was widely named among the best albums of 2014.

cocteau twins|sugar hiccup.fact: "Sugar Hiccup" appeared on both Cocteau Twins' 1983 album Head over Heels and the companion EP Sunburst and Snowblind, released that same year on 4AD. It's notable within the band's catalog for having actual discernible English lyrics, unlike much of their famously abstract vocal style, and it ranked 14th on John Peel's 1983 Festive Fifty countdown.

r.e.m.|imitation of life.fact: "Imitation of Life" was the lead single from R.E.M.'s 2001 album Reveal, written by Peter Buck, Mike Mills, and Michael Stipe and produced by the band with Pat McCarthy. Its title is borrowed from Douglas Sirk's 1959 film of the same name, used as a metaphor for the push and pull between adolescence and adulthood, and the song topped charts across the UK and mainland Europe while reaching the US Top 10 on rock radio.

tom waits|16 shells from a thirty-ought-.fact: "16 Shells From a Thirty-Ought-Six" is the second track on Tom Waits' 1983 album Swordfishtrombones, his first self-produced record and a major stylistic turn toward clattering, junkyard-orchestra arrangements. Waits said he wanted the track to have a chain-gang, work-song feel, built from metallic clangs and crashes meant to evoke the sound of a moving train.

the smile|foreign spies.fact: The Smile is the side project of Radiohead's Thom Yorke and Jonny Greenwood together with drummer Tom Skinner, who first worked with Greenwood scoring the 2012 film The Master. Greenwood invited Skinner to jam in 2018, and the pair brought in Yorke a few months later to complete the trio. "Foreign Spies" comes from their 2024 album Cutouts, recorded during the same sessions as its predecessor Wall of Eyes, partly at Abbey Road Studios.

kevin morby|parade.fact: "Parade" comes from Kevin Morby's 2014 album Still Life, and it works as a tribute to one of his musical heroes, Lou Reed, with a nod to Reed tucked into the lyrics. The album's title and cover art were actually borrowed from an art piece by Maynard Monrow called "Still Life with the Rejects from the Land of Misfit Toys," which gets referenced again in the song's closing lines. The track features a small chorus of guest singers alongside Morby and was produced by Rob Barbato.

sweeping promises|pain without a touch.fact: Sweeping Promises recorded "Pain Without a Touch" in November 2021, tracking part of it inside a repurposed bathroom at the band's home for its natural reverb. The song became the Massachusetts post-punk duo's first release after signing to Sub Pop, co-released with Feel It Records. Its hard-picked bassline and sparse, splashy guitar work made it an instant college-radio favorite.

the national|the system only dreams in t.fact: This lead single from The National's 2017 album Sleep Well Beast features something rare for the band: an honest-to-goodness guitar solo from Aaron Dessner. The National usually spreads the spotlight evenly across its members instead of letting one player take over, which makes the fuzzed-out solo here stand out. The album was recorded at Dessner's converted barn studio in New York's Hudson Valley and went on to win the Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album.

real estate|it's real.fact: "It's Real" is the sunny, surf-tinged highlight from Real Estate's 2011 album Days, the New Jersey band's first release for Domino Records. It was written by guitarists Martin Courtney and Matt Mondanile and produced by Kevin McMahon. With its easy, singalong "whoa-oh-oh" chorus, it's one of the clearest examples of the band's breezy jangle-pop sound.

toro y moi|baby drive it down.fact: "Baby Drive It Down" is a highlight from Toro y Moi's 2019 album Outer Peace, built around a marimba-like synth loop pulsing over a steady kick drum. Chaz Bear runs his vocals through heavy auto-tune and doubles the track, giving it a deliberately robotic feel. It's a good showcase of how Bear blends chillwave atmosphere with dance-pop structure.

new order|dreams never end.fact: "Dreams Never End" opens New Order's 1981 debut album Movement, and it's sung by bassist Peter Hook rather than the band's usual lead vocalist, Bernard Sumner. Hook's melodic, foregrounded basslines on this track became a blueprint for the sound that would carry New Order onto dance floors for the rest of the decade. Even the title is a callback to the band's earlier incarnation, echoing a lyric from the song "Insight."

future islands|sail.fact: "Sail" started life as a tour-only 7-inch single before landing on Future Islands' 2026 rarities collection, From a Hole in the Floor to a Fountain of Youth, released to mark the band's 20th anniversary. Bassist William Cashion put together the compilation's tracklist and picked its title. It gives longtime fans a chance to finally hear a batch of songs that had never been on streaming services before.

mamalarky|anhedonia.fact: Mamalarky singer Livvy Bennett and drummer Dylan Hill actually met back in middle school band class, and they'd already been making music with multi-instrumentalist Michael Hunter since high school by the time the group came together in Austin. Bassist Noor Khan joined later after Bennett put out a call for a bassist on, of all places, Tinder. Even the band's name came from a word-association game: roommates jotted down random words while the group jammed, and "Mamalarky" just stuck.

sharp pins|live without her love.fact: "Live Without Her Love" is Sharp Pins' cover of a song by the English mod-revival band Squire, cut for the 2026 tribute album Mod Mayday 23, a loving homage to the classic 1979 mod compilation Mods Mayday '79. Sharp Pins is the lo-fi power-pop solo project of Chicago musician Kai Slater, who also plays in Lifeguard and Dwaal Troupe.

hatchie|sage.fact: For her 2025 album Liquorice, Hatchie chose to work with just one outside collaborator, and she wanted that person to be a producer who also fronts their own band. That search led her to Jay Som, who recorded "Sage" at her own home studio with Warpaint and Courtney Barnett drummer Stella Mozgawa behind the kit. Hatchie's real-life partner, Joe Agius, co-wrote the track alongside her.

bat for lashes|all your gold.fact: While recording "All Your Gold" for 2012's The Haunted Man, Natasha Khan and producer Dan Carey got an unusual percussion sound by filling glasses with water and striking them with forks, a session Khan says took forever because the two of them kept cracking up laughing. Khan called this one the "difficult teenager" of the record, since it wouldn't come together for months. She eventually scrapped an early version entirely and rewrote it in a new key with a new chorus before it finally clicked.

the war on drugs|under the pressure.fact: "Under the Pressure" opens The War on Drugs' 2014 album Lost in the Dream with nearly nine minutes of slow-building krautrock groove, starting with ticking electronics and closing out with over two minutes of swirling, synchronized feedback. The track sets the tone for an album steeped in '80s heartland rock and motorik rhythm. At that length, it's one of the longest tracks the Philadelphia band has ever used to open an album.

black midi|chondromalacia patella.fact: black midi named this Cavalcade single after a real medical condition, chondromalacia patella, a type of knee pain from worn cartilage that one of the band members developed from running. Frontman Geordie Greep built the song's lyrics around that experience of pushing through pain on a run and then recovering from it. It's one of the more unusual song titles to come out of the UK's experimental rock scene.

suki waterhouse|dream woman.fact: "Dream Woman" was Suki Waterhouse's first solo single after her album Memoir of a Sparklemuffin, released through Sub Pop in 2025. She co-wrote the track with Natalie Findlay, with production from Jules Apollinaire. Waterhouse kept the project in the family, tapping her sister Imogen Waterhouse to direct the music video, with another sister, Madeleine, working as cinematographer.

king gizzard and the lizard wizard|le ri.fact: "Le Risque" is the lead single from King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard's 2024 album Flight b741, and it's also the first lead-vocal turn for the band's drummer, Michael "Cavs" Cavanagh. Built on a twangy, rockabilly-tinged guitar and harmonica backbeat, the song makes its case for living a little dangerously, name-checking thrill-seekers like daredevil Evel Knievel and tightrope walker Philippe Petit. The band says the whole album was made with no overarching concept, just a goal of keeping things fun and instinctual.

belle and sebastian|what happened to you.fact: This song was actually written for Belle and Sebastian's 2023 album Late Developers but got cut at the last minute because the record ran one track too long. Frontman Stuart Murdoch wrote it looking back at his own late teens, a rough stretch when he was struggling at university while living and breathing the music of that era. Despite its wistful, questioning title, the song ends on a hopeful note about finding a way forward.

diiv|the fountain.fact: "The Fountain" introduced DIIV's 2026 album ZIRP!, produced by A.G. Cook, best known for his work with Charli XCX and Caroline Polachek. Cook originally planned to chop up and rebuild the band's demos, but he scrapped that approach once he got obsessed with DIIV's live sound, insisting on tracking real drums before some songs were even finished. The result keeps DIIV's hazy, guitar-driven signature while pushing the production in a sharper direction.

bodega|tarkovski.fact: The title "Tarkovski" is BODEGA's pun on Russian filmmaker Andrei Tarkovsky, inspired by his book Sculpting in Time; the band was amused that Tarkovsky often broke his own stated rules of filmmaking. It's the lead single from their 2024 album Our Brand Could Be Yr Life, itself a riff on Michael Azerrad's famous book about the American underground rock scene, Our Band Could Be Your Life. The song's video even restages a famous candle-carrying scene from Tarkovsky's film Nostalghia before swerving into straight-up pop choreography.

cut worms|evil twin.fact: "Evil Twin" comes from Cut Worms' 2026 album Transmitter, which bandleader Max Clarke recorded with Jeff Tweedy producing at Wilco's Chicago studio, the Loft. Clarke says the song plays with pairs of opposites, mixing city and suburban imagery with ideas about public versus private selves. Musically it leans on jangly, heartache-laced guitars in the vein of The Replacements before dissolving into accordion and the sound of city sirens.

yard act|petroleum.fact: Yard Act's James Smith wrote 'Petroleum' after losing his patience on stage at a gig in Bognor Regis, telling the crowd flat-out he was bored -- a move that got him a stern talking-to from bandmate Ryan Needham. It sent him down a rabbit hole about what touring actually requires, and how fans often want a performed version of honesty rather than the real thing. That idea lands in the song's refrain about the soul needing 'petroleum' just to keep running. It's off 2024's 'Where's My Utopia?', which found the Leeds post-punk band leaning into a more electronic, psychedelic sound.

saintseneca|may day.fact: 'May Day' comes from Saintseneca's 2025 album Highwalllow & Supermoon Songs, the Columbus, Ohio band's first release in seven years. It's actually a 21-track project split into three sections -- a core album called Highwalllow orbited by two shorter 'moons' -- and 'May Day' lands on the Viridian Moon half. Songwriter Zac Little built the sprawling record with longtime collaborator Glenn Davis, with Bright Eyes' Mike Mogis handling the mix.

japanese breakfast|savage good boy.fact: The music video for Japanese Breakfast's 'Savage Good Boy' stars Michael Imperioli -- Christopher from The Sopranos -- opposite frontwoman Michelle Zauner. The song appears on 2021's Jubilee, the album that pushed Japanese Breakfast into the mainstream and landed a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Album. Musically, the track is built on bouncing drums and a bright, bubbly bassline, a deliberately upbeat sound Zauner designed as a stark contrast to the song's lyrics.

big thief|century.fact: Big Thief's 'Century' comes from 2022's sprawling double album Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You, which the band pieced together across four completely different recording sessions. They tracked in a barn in upstate New York, a canyon house in Topanga, a cabin in the Colorado Rockies, and a studio in Tucson, Arizona, over about five months. All told, they wrote and recorded 45 songs before narrowing things down to the final tracklist.

wednesday|how can you live if you can't.fact: Wednesday's Karly Hartzman has described 'How Can You Live If You Can't Love How Can You If You Do' as 'a Big Star-esque love song concocted around a James Baldwin quote' from his novel Another Country. It's a notable stylistic left turn for the Asheville band, trading their usual buzzsaw guitars and feedback for twangy pedal steel and gentle acoustic tones. The track appears on 2021's Twin Plagues.

molly burch feat. wild nothing|emotion.fact: Molly Burch traveled from Austin to Virginia to work with Wild Nothing's Jack Tatum, and the result was 'Emotion,' a disco-tinged dance track built after Burch shared her favorite pop songs with him. Burch has said the song is about feeling the full spectrum of emotions and using that sensitivity as fuel for something positive. It marked her first new release after a run of quieter, more subdued records.

wilco|hot sun.fact: Wilco's 'Hot Sun' comes from the Hot Sun Cool Shroud EP, a 2024 release built from material recorded during the sessions for their album Cousin. The track leans into rolling, twangy guitars that echo the band's alt-country roots from the 1990s. Lyrically, it follows Jeff Tweedy's recurring theme of searching for meaning, framed against the image of an oppressive, inescapable sun.

talking heads|heaven.fact: David Byrne has said the title of Talking Heads' 'Heaven' was actually borrowed from a real bar of the same name in the UK. In the song, heaven gets reimagined as a place where the same party and the same kiss repeat forever -- 'a place where nothing ever happens.' It appears on 1979's Fear of Music, the album where the band's arty, anxious sound really came into focus.

sam fender|people watching.fact: The title track from Sam Fender's album People Watching gave the Geordie singer his third straight UK Number One album, with the biggest opening week for a British act since Harry Styles' Harry's House. The album also broke the 21st-century record for fastest-selling vinyl release by a UK artist, moving 43,000 vinyl copies in its first week. The single itself reached the UK top five and went Platinum.

temples|vendetta.fact: Temples' 'Vendetta' marks a hard left turn for the English psych-rock band, swapping their usual retro guitar sound for a pulsing dance-floor groove. Frontman James Bagshaw described it as opening with 'an almost Justice-Daft Punk-sounding sample' before shifting into something closer to a modern David Guetta or Avicii track. It's the lead single from their album Bliss, the follow-up to 2023's Exotico.

waxahatchee|where's your love now.fact: 'Where's Your Love Now' is actually a cover -- Katie Crutchfield, who records as Waxahatchee, fell for the song by songwriter Nate Amos of This Is Lorelei and called it 'one of the best songs I've ever heard.' Her studio version even features Amos himself singing backing vocals. Crutchfield had been performing the song live for a while before officially releasing her take.

the shins|sleeping lessons.fact: James Mercer has said 'Sleeping Lessons' was 'loosely based on a number of jobs I've had,' inspired by watching coworkers stay stuck in lives of drudgery they didn't have to accept. Musically, he built the song's guitar line as a twist on a blues run inspired by 1960s singer Gary 'U.S.' Bonds. It opens the Shins' 2007 album Wincing the Night Away, a title that nods to Mercer's long bout of insomnia.

mary in the junkyard|new muscles.fact: 'New Muscles' by mary in the junkyard was written on accordion, and the lyrics are about as low-stakes as it gets -- bandmate David joining a gym. The music video, though, is no joke: bandmates Clari Freeman-Taylor and Saya Barbaglia spent a full year training in Muay Thai so the fight scene in the video could be real. It's a single from the London trio's debut album, Role Model Hermit.

beth gibbons|floating on a moment.fact: 'Floating On A Moment' was the first taste of Lives Outgrown, Portishead singer Beth Gibbons' solo debut album, which took about a decade to finish. She made the record with Simian Mobile Disco's James Ford and former Talk Talk drummer Lee Harris producing. The album marked a real departure from Portishead's trip-hop sound and went on to earn a Mercury Prize nomination.

khruangbin|mr. white.fact: 'Mr. White' is the instrumental opening track on Khruangbin's 2015 debut album, The Universe Smiles Upon You. With no lyrics beyond a looping, whispered 'white cat, white cat,' the Houston trio lets the song's smoky, jazz-lounge groove do all the talking. Fans have long pointed out the title's nod to Harvey Keitel's character in Reservoir Dogs, fitting for a band that builds instrumental worlds out of cinematic atmosphere.

grizzly bear|mourning sound.fact: 'Mourning Sound' is one of the most propulsive tracks Grizzly Bear ever made, built around a slinky bassline that recalls New Order. It started life as a guitar riff from Chris Taylor, with Daniel Rossen later adding the chorus. Its music video features a group of women performing a stylized dance ritual through a mansion, which the band described as a playful commentary on women's liberation. It comes from 2017's Painted Ruins.

toro y moi|daria (feat. kenny beats).fact: 'Daria' marked the first official studio collaboration between Toro y Moi and producer Kenny Beats, following Toro y Moi's guest appearance on Kenny's online freestyle show The Cave back in 2022. The song actually started as a Japan-only bonus track tied to Toro y Moi's album Hole Erth before getting a full standalone release. It dropped in the middle of a North American tour Toro y Moi was running alongside Panda Bear.

father john misty|the x-panded universe.fact: The title of Father John Misty's 'The X-panded Universe' plays on 'expanded universe,' the term used for the sprawling side-stories built around franchises like Star Wars or classic comic books. True to that idea, Josh Tillman fills the song with a comic-book-style plot -- a scientist, a hidden weapon, a far-off resistance camp -- told in his usual sweeping, orchestral style. It continues his run of genre-bending, theatrically arranged songwriting under the Father John Misty name.

queens of the stone age|insignificant ot.fact: Queens of the Stone Age's Josh Homme has described 'Insignificant Other' as being about how someone can feel like your whole world and then simply vanish from it, and the strange vertigo of being on the receiving end of that disappearance. Musically, the track leans toward a warmer, bluesier, more classic-rock sound compared to the band's usual riff-heavy attack. It's from Perfecth, the band's follow-up to 2023's In Times New Roman...

adrianne lenker|once a bunch.fact: 'Once A Bunch' started life as a bonus track tucked onto the Japanese CD release of Adrianne Lenker's solo album Bright Future before she gave it a proper standalone release. It was recorded during the same sessions as the album with producer Phil Weinrobe, featuring Mat Davidson and Josefin Runsteen. The country-tinged tune has a loose, warm feel that fits right alongside the rest of Bright Future.

black belt eagle scout|loss & relax.fact: Katherine Paul, who records as Black Belt Eagle Scout, wrote 'Loss & Relax' while thinking about the ferries that carry people across the Salish Sea near her home in the Swinomish Indian Tribal Community. She's said she was reflecting on how canoes -- a traditional form of transportation for her people -- have given way to ferries over time, and how that links past and present. The song closes on a note of resilience, picturing her community continuing to thrive on its ancestral waters.

bolis pupul|completely half.fact: 'Completely Half' is the lead single from Bolis Pupul's debut album Letter To Yu, co-produced by Soulwax and released on their Deewee label. Pupul, who's of both Belgian and Chinese heritage, built the song around the line 'completely half on my behalf,' playing with the math of a mixed identity. The video, shot on the streets of Hong Kong, was directed by acclaimed Magnum photographer Bieke Depoorter.

king gizzard and the lizard wizard|work.fact: "Work This Time" comes from King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's 2014 B-sides collection Oddments. Despite being released in 2014, the Melbourne band didn't actually play it live until November 2018, debuting it at The Tivoli in Brisbane. Since then it's become an occasional live cut, sometimes stretched out with extra guitar soloing.

julien baker and torres|tuesday.fact: "Tuesday" comes from Send a Prayer My Way, the first collaborative album from Julien Baker and TORRES (Mackenzie Scott), who'd talked about teaming up ever since sharing a bill at Chicago's Lincoln Hall back in 2016. The pair built the record around classic country storytelling and co-produced it with Sarah Tudzin of Illuminati Hotties over a couple of quick studio stints. Baker was such a night owl during the sessions that she'd sneak back into the files at 3 a.m. to add things like a banjo solo.

destroyer|june.fact: Destroyer's "June" arrived as a single from 2022's Labyrinthitis, and its video took the step-by-step "process video" format somewhere strange: it's a tutorial on making a burrito, which then gets delivered to frontman Dan Bejar by a figure in a full metallic suit. Bejar co-directed the clip himself with David Galloway. He's also said the song's sprawling back half includes passages that would never have made it onto earlier Destroyer records.

mitski|two slow dancers.fact: "Two Slow Dancers" closes out Mitski's 2018 album Be the Cowboy, picturing two former sweethearts reuniting years later for one last dance in a high school gymnasium. It's one of the quieter, more stripped-down moments on a record otherwise built around a tightly wound, controlled persona Mitski created for the album. Critics singled it out as among the most affecting songs of her career.

fiona apple|i want you to love me.fact: "I Want You to Love Me" opens Fiona Apple's 2020 album Fetch the Bolt Cutters, which she recorded in her own home studio instead of a commercial facility, with a band that included drummer Amy Aileen Wood, bassist Sebastian Steinberg, and multi-instrumentalist David Garza. About a minute in, Apple holds a single note far longer than expected, then holds it longer still, before the song builds into its full piano-driven swell.

the sugarcubes|birthday.fact: "Birthday" was The Sugarcubes' first international single, and it came together almost by accident: after a festival promoter couldn't pay the band for a gig, he offered them free studio time instead, and this song is what they wrote with it. Released in 1987, it introduced a young Bjork to audiences outside Iceland and topped John Peel's Festive Fifty list that year.

talking heads|crosseyed and painless.fact: "Crosseyed and Painless" was tracked for 1980's Remain in Light at Compass Point Studios in Nassau, with vocals and overdubs finished later at Sigma Sound in New York. Guitarist Adrian Belew happened to be passing through on tour with David Bowie and ended up recording all his guitar parts for the entire album in a single session. The music video skips the band altogether in favor of the Electric Boogaloos breakdance crew, directed by Toni Basil.

tame impala|apocalypse dreams.fact: "Apocalypse Dreams" was the first song Kevin Parker ever co-wrote for Tame Impala, working with keyboardist Jay Watson on an album, Lonerism, that he otherwise recorded almost entirely alone. Parker says he wrote the lyrics before ever seeing the 2011 film Melancholia, then was startled by how closely its themes lined up once he finally watched it. The track kicked off Lonerism's promotional rollout as its first single in mid-2012.

beach house|10-37.fact: Beach House recorded "10:37" during an unusual session that produced two full albums at once, Depression Cherry and Thank Your Lucky Stars, holed up at Studio in the Country in Bogalusa, Louisiana, over the winter of 2014 into 2015.
